Bio-layer interferometry (BLI) and non-denaturing polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE) analyses demonstrate that substituting T with s 2 U at the N-terminal position adjacent to Q (P3-2QT) enhances binding affinity by ∼10-fold compared to unmodified P3, whereas C-terminal substitution (P3-TQ2) yields only a 2-fold improvement. Consistent with these findings, a cell-free dual-luciferase reporter assay reveals that P3-2QT significantly increases ribosomal frameshifting efficiency compared to P3 and P3-TQ2. Molecular dynamics simulations further indicate that P3-2QT maintains enhanced PNA-PNA stacking stability, particularly between s 2 U3 and Q4, suggesting a structural basis for its superior activity. Intriguingly, analogous s 2 U substitution in the P5 oligomer with the Q replaced by L does not confer a comparable enhancement in binding to the target RNA (rHP1) and frameshifting stimulation, highlighting the context-dependent nature of this modification. To assess the broader applicability of the s 2 U-Q motif, we examined its effect in dbPNAs targeting the RNA panhandle structure of influenza virus A and precursor microRNA-21, respectively. Both PAGE and BLI data confirm that s 2 U incorporation improves binding affinity, reinforcing the generality of this strategy. These findings underscore the potential of sequence-dependent uracil thiolation in optimizing triplex-forming dsRNA-binding PNAs, warranting further exploration of modified nucleobase designs to enhance their binding and functional properties. Graphical abstract Highlights Thiolation of uracil upstream of Q base in PNA markedly enhances triplex binding affinity and enables isoenergetic and orthogonal targeting/activation. N-terminal s 2 U modification adjacent to Q residues increases PNA-dsRNA binding by ∼10-fold and significantly boosts ribosomal frameshifting efficiency. Biophysical assays and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that thiolation improves PNA stacking stability and slows dissociation, thereby enhancing functional activity toward structured RNA targets. The general applicability of s 2 U modification is demonstrated with influenza A virus RNA panhandle structure and precursor micoRNA-21 targets, underscoring its broad potential for optimizing PNA-based therapeutics and biotechnological tools.

title: Open-source chemoinformatics platforms for multi-target structure-activity relationships
abstract: Structure-activity relationships (SARs) are fundamental in medicinal chemistry, linking chemical structure with biological activity. However, many diseases involve multiple targets and pathways, making polypharmacology a key consideration. Traditional SAR approaches consider one target at a time, but the scale and complexity of modern screening data demand integrative methods. Chemoinformatic methods have been adapted to mine structure-multiple activity relationships (SMARTs) from large multi-target datasets, enabling analysis of compounds across multiple assays simultaneously. In this review, we map the current "SMART toolbox" of open-source chemoinformatics platforms, highlighting twelve tools that link chemical structures to diverse biological activities and provide integrative data-visualization capabilities. For each platform, we note open-source availability to promote reproducibility. Collectively, these platforms enable integrative visualization and analysis of multi-target activity landscapes, accelerating discovery of multi-functional therapeutics. Finally, we illustrate these approaches in a peptide design case study, showing how SMARTs analysis can guide the engineering of multi-functional bioactive compounds.

title: Hybrid geothermal-wind integration in the US energy grid
abstract: Here, we combine US wind generation—a cheap yet intermittent source of electricity—with the latest geothermal resource estimates to understand the technoeconomic possibilities of pairing enhanced geothermal systems (EGSs) with existing wind farms to develop a hybrid energy system. Using observed generation data from 583 wind farms, generation gaps are quantified and geographically paired with the latest EGS estimates. Results demonstrate that EGS potential within a 1 km 2 footprint can supplement wind generation at 56% of onshore wind farms. Each wind farm can be supplemented by EGSs when 10% of its surface-occupying footprint is available. The cost of EGSs at wind farms is lowest in the western US and southern Texas border and highest in the central US. While further experiments are warranted, a wind + EGS hybrid system offers an opportunity to increase power output from the same land footprint while maximizing the use of existing electrical infrastructure.

title: Chiral sulfonimidoyl fluorides display potent stereoselective inhibition of chymotrypsin
abstract: Herein, we present chiral sulfonimidoyl fluorides as enantioselective inhibitors of α-chymotrypsin. After screening a library of 16 racemic sulfonimidoyl fluorides for their inhibitory potential for this well-studied model serine protease, we enantiomerically separated the five best-performing inhibitors and determined the IC 50 values of the enantiomers. We not only find enantioselective inhibition but also that the most potent derivatives are >25 times more active than the established serine protease inhibitor, PMSF. Furthermore, tryptic digestion and mass spectrometry (MS) analysis reveal covalent modification of the active site serine, and molecular docking simulations corroborate the determined IC 50 values. In view of the crucial role of serine proteases in the regulation of many biological processes, we expect that this class of inhibitors can occupy an important place in future endeavors to fight diseases.

title: Catalytic resonance theory for the kinetic signatures of multiple wavelength photocatalysis
abstract: Multi-step surface chemistry promoted with one or two wavelengths of light exhibited distinct kinetic signatures indicative of the light-adsorbate interactions and the number of photon-sensitive elementary steps. In this work, kinetic Monte Carlo simulations identified the kinetic response of general surface mechanisms to variation in the per-site photon flux of one or two wavelengths of incident light. Photocatalytic rates were described via a non-dimensional photon flux, identifying multiple kinetic regimes with unique degrees of rate control. Under photon-controlled kinetic conditions, maximum quantum yield and turnover frequency were obtained under constant illumination, while pulsing of one or more light sources was shown to exhibit slower rates and less efficient photocatalytic promotion due to the inherent dynamic nature of light, which comprises a stream of photons. Simulations provided distinct kinetic signatures in catalytic rates and Arrhenius kinetics for specific light-surface-adsorbate interactions corresponding to photocatalytic promotion of specific steps in surface chemistry.

title: Living cement for microbial intelligence
abstract: Cement and concrete have long been regarded as an inert material designed solely for human needs: structural strength, durability, and more recently, low-carbon performance. Yet emerging evidence shows that microbial life can survive, adapt, and function within the alkaline and evolving microstructure of cement. This discovery opens an entirely new design paradigm that cement as a scaffold for microbial activity rather than a barrier to it. In this perspective, we review the rapidly expanding field of microbial cement composites, encompassing self-healing through biomineralization, biologically accelerated carbonation and CO₂ sequestration, electroactive and energy-storing systems, corrosion-mitigating microbial interfaces, and microbially enabled sensing and responsiveness. Across these diverse functions, a consistent insight emerges, microbial performance is fundamentally constrained by the chemical, spatial, and hydration-driven dynamics of cement. These constraints highlight the need for a shift from placing microbes into conventional cement toward designing cementitious materials that actively support microbial metabolism, signaling, and long-term viability. We outline the scientific principles required to engineer cement as a microbial habitat, and we explore future directions including genetically engineered strains, extremophiles, synthetic microbial consortia, fungal and hybrid bioelectronic systems. Together, these directions point toward a new class of living cementitious materials in which structural performance, environmental functions, and microbial intelligence evolve within a single, co-designed mineral-biological system.

title: Developing ChemMLLM as a multimodal large language model for chemistry
abstract: Recent years have seen rapid progress in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in the field of chemistry. However, chemical MLLMs capable of handling cross-modal understanding and generation remain underexplored. To fill this gap, we propose ChemMLLM, a unified chemical MLLM for molecule understanding and generation. In this work, we design five types of multimodal tasks across text, molecular simplified molecular input line entry system (SMILES) strings, and images and curate the datasets. We benchmark ChemMLLM against a range of general leading MLLMs, chemical LLMs, and specialized models on these tasks. Experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of a unified multimodal interface. Our work extends the capabilities of chemical MLLMs to the realm of image generation, demonstrating the feasibility of unifying multiple cross-modal chemical tasks within a single mode l and enabling more intuitive, visual human-artificial intelligence (AI) interaction.

title: Cellular mechano-memory informs biomaterials and mechano-medicine
abstract: Mechano-memory refers to the ability of cells to encode mechanical experiences as short- and long-term regulatory states that shape cellular behavior and tissue function. By influencing cell-fate decisions, immune responses, tissue regeneration, and disease evolution, mechano-memory serves as a foundational principle for biological research, a guiding framework for biomaterials and bioengineering design, and a key determinant of therapeutic performance. In clinical contexts, interventions that account for cellular mechanical memory provide a route toward more durable and personalized treatments by aligning engineered microenvironments with patient- and tissue-specific mechanical histories. In this review, we outline the biological basis of mechano-memory and summarize how engineered mechanical environments across multiple dimensional scales regulate its formation and persistence, highlighting translational opportunities and remaining challenges.

title: Contact lens bioelectronic platform for non-invasive depression treatment with machine-learning-based evaluation
abstract: Here, we present a wearable, non-invasive contact lens bioelectronic platform designed to enable a more fundamental treatment of depression. Through the implementation of temporal-interference-based transcorneal electrical stimulation (TI-TES), the contact lens platform enables effective delivery of stimulation from the corneal surface to the retina and ultimately to the brain. The TI-TES platform features ultrathin gallium oxide and platinum layers as transparent, flexible electrodes, enabling seamless integration into soft contact lenses. This approach preserves vision and ensures conformal ocular coupling. In a preclinical stress-induced mouse model that recapitulates key behavioral and biological features associated with depression, TI-TES enhanced behavioral resilience, restored prefrontal-hippocampal oscillatory synchrony, and normalized depression-related biomarkers. Machine-learning integration of behavioral, electrophysiological, and biological data consistently distinguished treated from control groups. These preclinical findings establish TI-TES as a non-invasive bioelectronic strategy that overcomes current limitations, enabling selective eye-brain pathway modulation for depression and potentially other brain disorders.

title: Moisture-swing CO2 capture from air enabled by graphene oxide for agricultural applications
abstract: The moisture-swing technique is an effective strategy for directly capturing CO 2 from ambient air. However, adsorption capacity and efficiency of moisture-swing sorbents are limited due to the low specific surface area and lack of porous channels within the materials. Here, we synthesize a graphene oxide sorbent with a specific surface area as high as 107 m 2 g −1 and abundant mesopores within the material. The sorbent delivers a large CO 2 adsorption capacity of 1.354 mmol g −1 under precise control, exceeding most of other similar sorbents. It is mainly attributed to the fast CO 2 diffusion channels (mesopores and surface area) and numerous adsorption sites (oxygen-containing groups) provided by graphene oxide. The sorbent displays excellent working stability with negligible capacity degradation even after 1,000 repeated capture-release cycles. Further, we have demonstrated plant growth promotion of the moisture-swing technique by producing local high CO 2 concentration with our graphene oxide sorbents.

title: Hemiprotonated cytosine–cytosine base pairs control excited state dynamics in human telomere and c-MYC promoter i-motifs
abstract: i-Motifs are tetra-stranded DNA structures stabilized by hemiprotonated cytosine–cytosine base pairs, with emerging roles in gene regulation and nanotechnology. Here, we present the first comprehensive comparative study of class I and II i-motifs from human telomeric and MYC0 promoter sequences. Using ultrafast broadband fluorescence, fluorescence anisotropy, and transient absorption spectroscopy, we uncover unprecedented intra-pair charge-transfer excimers that form within sub-picoseconds and deactivate over several hundred picoseconds via bridging proton transfer. These unusually long-lived, weakly emissive excimers uniquely account for the intrinsic red-shifted fluorescence of i-motifs, with lifetimes and yields dictated by structural heterogeneity, the number of hemiprotonated base pairs, and cooperative proton relocation. Crucially, i-motif excited-state dynamics are governed solely by interdigitated hemiprotonated base pairing, in sharp contrast to double-stranded DNA and guanine quadruplexes, where both stacking and pairing interactions operate. These findings redefine nucleic acid excited-state behavior and highlight the potential of i-motif fluorescence for label-free biosensing and nanotechnology.

title: Engineering a dietary fiber-based injectable hydrogel for blood-clotting applications
abstract: Excessive blood loss from traumatic injuries or even routine surgical procedures is a major concern, and without proper wound closure, it can turn fatal. In this work, we have developed an entirely bio-based, sustainable hydrogel, pGel, for managing excessive blood loss. Psyllium, a plant-derived, naturally occurring, biocompatible, and biodegradable polysaccharide, was used as the primary polymer. Gelatin, a mammalian collagen-derived protein with biocompatibility, biodegradability, and favorable cell-adhesive properties, was used as an additive to improve the bioactivity of pGel. The carefully optimized pGel displayed favorable injectability and recovery under a cyclic strain time sweep, making it a minimally invasive injectable bio-based platform. Furthermore, kaolin, a naturally occurring mineral aluminosilicate clay with rapid clotting properties, was used as the primary blood-clotting agent. The developed kaolin-incorporated hydrogel demonstrated superior clotting abilities and adequate cytocompatibility. Taken together, we believe that this bio-based injectable hydrogel will find potential use as an effective blood-clotting agent.

title: Advancing smart energy management with generative artificial intelligence
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) holds significant potential in mitigating the challenges posed by complexity and uncertainty in energy systems through its distinctive generative capabilities. It is transforming the management of power sources, grids, loads, and storage through shared functions including planning, forecasting and scenario generation, operation and control, diagnosis, and maintenance. Although there are considerable advantages for the application of generative AI in various aspects of the energy system, it remains crucial to deeply explore its actual capabilities and inherent limitations in smart energy management. In particular, we have distinguished between challenges that are generic to AI and those that are uniquely shaped by the physical, operational, and safety-critical nature of the energy system. Further advancements will depend on how effectively and safely generative AI can be aligned with physical laws while operating beyond the constraints of historical data, thus unlocking its full potential in energy systems.

title: The future of solar-driven water splitting
abstract: Solar-driven water splitting offers a direct path to green hydrogen by using sunlight to split water into hydrogen and oxygen, enabling flexible energy storage and hydrogen fuel production. Yet, turning lab-scale demonstrations into widespread deployment requires overcoming intertwined fundamental and engineering challenges. This Voices piece gathers researchers from around the world who work on photocatalytic, photoelectrochemical, and biophotoelectrochemical water splitting to discuss bottlenecks, promising strategies, and the tools most helpful for advancing solar fuels production. They address design principles for materials and devices, emerging configurations and benchmarking concepts, pathways to commercialization, and how related catalytic processes and adjacent fields can guide sustainable hydrogen evolution. What becomes clear is that achieving scalable solar-driven hydrogen production will require integrated, multi-disciplinary efforts that bridge responsible discovery and deployment.

title: Real-world VOC exposure and health implications in recreational vehicles under climate stress
abstract: Rising mobile living and frequent extreme climate events make recreational vehicles (RVs) a critical microenvironment with notable exposure risks. Here, we conduct field observations in an RV under sealed conditions by measuring the concentrations of 22 typical volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and examining the influence of environmental parameters on VOC dynamics and exposure risks. Results reveal long-tail characteristics of VOCs, dominated by formaldehyde (average concentration of 118.9 μg/m 3 ), that exceed the WHO guideline limit. Material surface temperature and external heat load are identified as key influencing factors of VOC dynamics. An interpretable deep learning model is developed to extract influencing factors and predict VOC change patterns. Risk assessment indicates that the potential risks from formaldehyde exposure in RVs are high among those of the reported vehicle types. By establishing an integrated framework incorporating real-world measurements, predictive modeling, and risk assessment, this study provides a basis for understanding VOC dynamics in mobile living environments.

title: Oxidation-induced mechanical weakening of virus particles by antiviral coatings
abstract: Oxidation is a widely used strategy for inactivating microbes, including viruses. However, how oxidative processes affect the structural integrity of viral capsids remains poorly understood. Here, we explore the biomechanical effects of oxidation on tobacco mild green mosaic virus exposed to virucidal surfaces. We compare three conditions: untreated virions, virions incubated on an inert control surface, and virions exposed to a reactive surface containing N-chloro hydantoin. Using atomic force microscopy, we assess changes in surface topography and capsid biomechanics. Our results show that oxidized particles maintain their external appearance but exhibit reduced stiffness and breaking force. Notably, viral RNA remains intact, suggesting that oxidation only affects capsid components. Complementary computational modeling suggests a possible capsid site where N-chloro hydantoin induces destabilizing effects. Together, these findings offer new insights into how oxidative agents alter viral physical properties and suggest potential molecular targets for more effective antiviral coatings.

title: Boosting power output of microbial biofilm-based hydrovoltaic generator via surface polymerization
abstract: Microbial biofilm-based hydrovoltaic electricity generators (BioHEGs) exemplify low-cost and facile manufacturing platforms for hydrovoltaic energy, albeit with relatively low power output that is unsatisfactory for practical applications. Herein, in situ surface polymerization of polyaniline (PAni) on Shewanella oneidensis ( S. o ) is verified to boost the hydrovoltaic performance of the biohybrid system. Notably, the S. o @PAni BioHEG unit achieves an ultra-high stable power density of ca. 168.6 mW·m −2 , which outperforms all BioHEGs hitherto documented by an order of magnitude. Specifically, the output voltage and current density of S. o @PAni BioHEG are significantly enhanced due to the formation of Schottky junctions at the interface between the microbial biofilm and electrode. Moreover, the synergistic effect of extracellular polymeric substances and PAni induces accelerated electron transfer, thereby lowering the electrical resistance in the system. This work unambiguously provides a reliable strategy for advancing the performance of BioHEGs toward more comprehensive and practical scenarios.

title: High transmittance retention in Ce-free glass for space solar panels
abstract: Maintaining high transmittance is essential for cover glasses used in space solar cells exposed to radiation and sunlight. Here, we evaluate commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) cerium-undoped borosilicate glass as an alternative to conventional space-grade cerium-doped glass. We examine whether coloration induced by electron irradiation can recover under illumination simulated to match the air-mass-zero (AM0) spectrum. Electron irradiation tests identified three fluence regimes with different coloration characteristics, and each regime was evaluated using heat-light soaking (HLS) tests using spectral transmittance measurements. In addition, electron spin resonance (ESR) was employed to clarify the light-induced recovery mechanism, showing that precursor point defects that contribute to the occurrence of coloration disappear after HLS. The results from these simulated conditions indicate that concurrent radiation and light exposure can maintain high transmittance without performance-degrading coloration. These findings provide quantitative evidence that supports COTS cerium-undoped borosilicate glass as a viable cover-glass material, with potential benefits for cost reduction and supply-chain robustness.

title: AI-driven next-gen health monitoring via flexible sensors to decode breath
abstract: Respiratory dynamic patterns offer a unique window into the body's cardiorespiratory, metabolic, and neurological functions, yet continuous and accurate capture of such signals is fundamentally challenged by the mismatch between sensing interfaces and dynamic biological tissues. This review focuses on the convergence of flexible material innovations and artificial intelligence (AI) analytics to outline the development of next-generation intelligent respiratory monitoring. It systematically examines bioinspired flexible strain and humidity sensors with microstructural designs, elaborating on their medical-grade accuracy in quantifying respiratory parameters and the central role of material-device co-design in boosting sensing performance, comfort, and robustness. AI's function as a powerful signal decoder, enabling at-home lung function measurement, anomaly detection, and cross-disciplinary digital biomarker extraction for disease screening, is discussed. The review constructs a material-to-integration-to-intelligent interpretation technological paradigm advancing personalized medicine, envisions its value in chronic disease management and remote monitoring, and identifies key clinical translation challenges to provide forward-looking research perspectives.

title: Solar-driven device resilience in extreme terrestrial environments
abstract: Solar-driven chemical conversion systems offer scalable solutions for energy storage and water purification, yet their performance remains constrained by the controlled laboratory conditions in which they are tested. Deployment in extreme terrestrial environments (ETEs), characterized by thermal extremes, intermittent light, and fluctuations in photon flux, requires a shift from material-centric optimization to holistic device resilience. Herein, we propose a framework based on three core principles: kinetic decoupling, temporal bridging, and operational intelligence. When flexibly integrated, these strategies enable hybrid platforms to reach DTI 3–4 and chart a path toward scalable deployment (DTI-5). We advocate standardized translational metrics to quantify robustness and highlight future integration across terrestrial, marine, and extraterrestrial domains.

title: Molecular dynamics of reversible iron-catechol complexes as a toughening mechanism for mussel foot protein assemblies
abstract: Metal-catechol coordination is a principal design feature of mussel foot proteins (mfps) that facilitate tough underwater adhesion. Single-molecule models of metal-protein complexes cannot predict the outstanding cohesive properties of mussel-inspired adhesive interfaces because they lack the resolution at the scale of intermolecular networks. Here, we elucidate these dynamics by establishing a fully atomistic framework for modeling bulk mfp-inspired materials to observe the reversible dynamics of Fe 3+ -mediated catechol crosslinks. We first developed parameters for covalent and ionic crosslinks formed by catechol groups and validated them against quantum-mechanical studies. We then demonstrated how rupture and reformation of Fe 3 + -catechol crosslinks and DOPA deprotonation enhance the mechanical properties of the material. Correlating coordination dynamics with peaks in the sawtooth stress-strain curves ascertains the molecular origins of toughness in metal-coordinated biopolymers. These findings provide a predictive platform for designing sequence-defined mfp-inspired materials that are critically needed for wet bonding and surgical adhesives.

title: Explaining a molecular diffusion model
Recent advances in flexible bioelectronics and intelligent wearable devices for wound management
abstract: Large, non-healing, or chronic wounds are a global medical challenge that affects millions of patients. Currently, the effectiveness of clinical wound management is still limited by passive treatment strategies, which typically rely on physicians' experience and laboratory tests for qualitative assessments, resulting in prolonged hospitalization, increased patient suffering, and even more severe complications. In recent years, with the rapid development of flexible electronics and wearable devices, various types of bioelectronic dressings/bandages have been extensively explored and applied in wound management. This review aims to systematically review the latest advances in flexible electronics and intelligent wearable devices for wound monitoring and treatment. First, the progress of wound exudate management technology is introduced. Second, sensing of wound biomarkers, including material innovation, sensing mechanisms, and performance advantages, is summarized. Third, diverse therapeutic strategies integrated into wearable devices are reviewed, emphasizing the targeted and on-demand intervention capabilities. Fourth, integrated closed-loop systems that combine power supply, artificial intelligence assistance, and communication are discussed. Finally, the current challenges and future prospects are discussed. This review aims to provide comprehensive insights for researchers and clinicians engaged in the development and application of flexible electronics and intelligent wearable devices for wound care.

title: Role of electrode microstructure and kinetics in oscillations in Li-ion batteries revealed by phase-field simulations
abstract: In phase-separation electrodes of Li-ion batteries, a few particles carry the major share of the global current. This uneven distribution can, in turn, give rise to voltage oscillations, but the specifics of this process are not fully understood. Phase-field simulations may be used to investigate this behavior directly from the material's thermodynamics. Here, we report a model that goes beyond the pseudo-two-dimensional (P2D) representation, resolving particle-scale equations on a multidimensional mesh. Simulations confirm that this approach overcomes the limitations of lower-dimensional models. Results obtained with this simulation setup allowed two contributions to the battery community: evidencing that the oscillation behavior is closely linked to the active particle microstructure and demonstrating a quantitative relationship between oscillation properties and intercalation kinetic parameters. The former could be exploited as a resource-cheap protocol for electrode microstructure characterization, whereas the latter could be useful for battery-health assessment.

title: Photothermally enhanced ammonia synthesis and Zn-nitrite battery performance enabled by bimetallic Cu-Ni synergy
abstract: The electroreduction of nitrite (NO 2 − ) to ammonia (NH 3 ) offers dual benefits for resource valorization and wastewater remediation but suffers from limitations in active hydrogen (∗H) management and external energy utilization. Here, we report a photothermal electrocatalyst of Cu-Ni-FeOOH for efficient NO 2 − -to-NH 3 conversion. Experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that Ni centers promote water dissociation, supplying ∗H to adjacent Cu sites for NO 2 − hydrogenation. The catalyst achieves a high Faradaic efficiency of 98.6% with an NH 3 yield of 8.86 mg h −1 cm −2 at −0.1 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE). When exposed to near-infrared light irradiation, the in situ -generated thermal energy further enhances the electrocatalytic activity for NO 2 − reduction and improves the performance of a Zn-nitrite battery. This work provides a strategic direction for sustainable NH 3 synthesis through the design of advanced electrocatalytic systems synergistically coupled with external photothermal fields.

title: A multiscale framework for uncovering surfactant-mediated viral capsid disruption
abstract: Abstract Disinfection remains a critical strategy for controlling the transmission of infectious diseases. However, small non-enveloped viruses exhibit exceptional resistance to many disinfectants, often requiring harsh protein-disrupting chemicals for effective inactivation, thereby limiting their applicability in personal care products due to associated side effects. Sodium dodecyl sulphate (SDS) is a widely used anionic surfactant known for its virucidal efficacy; however, the molecular details of its action against robust non-enveloped viruses remain poorly understood, limiting efforts to design safer and more targeted antiviral formulations. In this study, a multiscale simulation approach combining a novel atomic-resolution icosahedral “scaffold framework” and coarse-grained modelling was developed to elucidate the mechanism of SDS-driven disruption of MS2 bacteriophage capsid, a surrogate for non-enveloped viruses. Experimental analyses including dynamic light scattering and transmission electron microscopy revealed that SDS inactivates MS2 in a strongly pH-dependent manner, triggering capsid disassembly at acidic pH while leaving particles largely intact at neutral pH. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated that SDS micelles preferentially associate with hexameric pores and inter-dimer clefts under acidic conditions, where protonation of acidic residues weakens the electrostatic network of the capsid surface. Together, these findings provide a detailed molecular framework for SDS virucidal action and highlight the importance of environmental pH in modulating surfactant–virus interactions. These insights offer a foundation for designing next-generation antiviral surfactants with improved efficacy and biocompatibility.

title: Tuning Ni/Al2O3 catalyst via Cu incorporation for selective deoxygenation and (de)methylation of guaiacol
abstract: Hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) of lignin-derived phenolics is a key strategy for producing renewable fuels and value-added chemicals. Conventional Ni/Al 2 O 3 catalysts lead to the formation of undesired saturated oxygenates, due to their high tendency toward aromatic-ring hydrogenation. Here, we report that Cu incorporation into Ni/Al 2 O 3 selectively tunes reaction pathways in guaiacol and anisole HDO. The resulting Ni-Cu/Al 2 O 3 catalysts suppress hydrogenation and (de)methylation to different extents. While anisole conversion shows minor selectivity changes, guaiacol exhibits a pronounced shift toward deoxygenation and methylation, due to stronger inhibition of hydrogenation. Kinetic modeling reveals unequal suppression of competing pathways and corresponding changes in rate-determining steps. Notably, the shift away from hydrogenated oxygenates toward deoxygenated and methylated products persists at elevated hydrogen pressures. At 270°C and 40 bar H 2 , 5% Ni-5% Cu/Al 2 O 3 achieves >70% guaiacol conversion, and this produces cyclohexane and methylated naphthenics and phenolics as primary products.

title: Chemical language models for generating compounds with triple-target activity
Comparative analysis of gamma peptide nucleic acid variants in targeting chromosomal DNA
Photocontrolled hERG channel blockade by diazirine integrated into BeKm-1 pharmacophore
abstract: Here we report that incorporation of diazirine-containing amino acids, including photoleucine and photomethionine, into the pharmacophore of the hERG blocker BeKm-1 enables optical control of peptide activity and, in specific cases, induces irreversible channel inhibition upon UV illumination. These analogs retain blocking activity in the dark while displaying light-dependent modulation of potency, reflecting dynamic reorganization of the pharmacophore. Notably, photoactivation can trigger covalent crosslinking to the channel under physiological conditions, resulting in prolonged inhibitory effects. This dual capability overcomes key limitations of peptide therapeutics, including rapid clearance and off-target effects, by enabling spatial and temporal control of activity at low concentrations. Our findings establish a generalizable photopharmacological strategy to tune peptide-target interactions and achieve tissue-restricted, on-demand therapeutic effects, opening new avenues for precision therapeutics.

title: A ligase-mediated encoding system for rapid, multiplex single-nucleotide variant detection
abstract: Accurate detection of single-nucleotide variants (SNV) is critical for genetic disease diagnosis and cancer profiling, yet existing methods often lack the combination of specificity, multiplexing capacity, and rapid workflow required for clinical application. Here, we report a ligase-mediated encoding (LmCo) system that integrates ligase chain reaction (LCR) for single-base discrimination with hybridization chain reaction (HCR) for signal amplification and multicolor fluorescence encoding. The system achieves a detection limit of 0.1626 fM and enables reliable identification of mutant alleles at frequencies as low as 0.0001% variant allele fraction, substantially outperforming conventional methods. LmCo simultaneously detects six or more SNV targets in a single closed-tube reaction with minimal crosstalk, demonstrates robust stability in complex matrices, and achieves 96.7% accuracy in simulated clinical samples. This platform provides a rapid, sensitive, and highly multiplexed solution for SNV detection in molecular diagnostics and precision medicine.

title: Predicting battery performance with small datasets by enhancing machine learning with distribution of relaxation times analysis
abstract: Accurate battery diagnostic models often struggle in capturing complex degradation mechanisms. Here, we report a combined approach using distribution of relaxation time (DRT) analysis and machine learning (ML) of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data to diagnose and predict the performance of solid-state batteries. The dataset has 112 impedance measurements collected over 100 cycles from eight TDK CeraCharge batteries. Using EIS features and the applied charge-discharge rate, the models estimate battery capacity at a given cycle and predict the capacity after the subsequent ten cycles. ML methods, including Bayesian regression, Gaussian process regression, neural networks, and decision trees, achieve accurate diagnostics (mean absolute error 1.6%) and prediction (2.4%). DRT-based feature selection identifies the most informative frequency range (15 Hz–1.5 kHz) and improves training efficiency. Tomography reveals mechanical degradation, i.e., volume expansion and fractures, which increases impedance and contributes to capacity loss. This approach enables accurate, data-driven battery diagnostics and forecasting.

title: Cell teardown and characterization of a Hina commercial sodium-ion battery
abstract: Transparent insight into the design and materials of commercial sodium-ion batteries is essential for assessing their maturity and benchmarking against lithium-ion technologies. We report postmortem analysis and electrochemical testing of the most commercialized sodium-ion battery technology from Hina Battery, which employs a tabless double-aluminum architecture and a novel cathode composition, NaCu 1/9 Ni 2/9 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 . This cathode features a distinctive spatial separation of copper from the other transition metals (Ni, Fe, and Mn) within individual particles. Using an Archimedean-spiral analysis of computed tomography data, we estimate total cathode length with 2% deviation, without additional image optimization. The cell delivers performance and production quality comparable to state-of-the-art Li-ion batteries: impedance variation across 120 cells is 5.3%, capacity remains over 100% at 4C (25°C), and usable discharge energy above 80% at −20°C, though this value drops to 56% in the charging direction.

title: EPR-refined atomistic molecular dynamics delivers predictive spectroscopy in self-organized soft matter systems
abstract: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy with nitroxide spin probes is a sensitive probe of structural dynamics in soft matter. Here, we report the use of EPR to test and refine atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) force fields for the discotic liquid crystal 2,3,6,7,10,11 hexa(hexyloxy)triphenylene (HAT6). We show that subtle variations in partial charge schemes, aromatic core Lennard-Jones interactions, and alkoxy torsional potentials cause pronounced changes in predicted EPR line shapes. By comparing experimental and MD-predicted spectra at a reference temperature, we identify refined parameters that reproduce both the measured spectra and the isotropic-columnar phase transition temperature. The predictions reveal pretransitional growth of short molecular stacks in the isotropic phase and the emergence of columnar order on cooling. This work establishes EPR spectroscopy as a powerful benchmark for testing and improving molecular force fields to deliver fully atomistic predictions of variable temperature EPR spectra of a discotic liquid crystal.

title: High-resolution imaging of cylindrical cells using curved-scintillator-based optically coupled X-ray computed tomography
abstract: X-ray computed tomography (CT) is widely used for nondestructive inspection of cylindrical lithium-ion batteries. However, in conventional flat-detector-based CT systems, spatial resolution is limited by focal-spot-induced blurring, which becomes severe at the cell periphery due to an increased object-to-detector distance. This is particularly problematic for cylindrical battery inspection, where resolving peripheral features such as electrode termination positions is essential. Here, we present a curved-scintillator-based optically coupled X-ray CT system that reduces the effective object-to-detector distance at the periphery, suppressing focal-spot-induced blurring while enabling the use of a high-power X-ray tube. The system is experimentally demonstrated through CT imaging of a 4680 cylindrical lithium-ion cell. The curved scintillator improves peripheral spatial resolution by approximately 8% compared with the flat-scintillator configuration, providing more uniform resolution across the field of view. Frequency- and image-domain resolution analyses confirm the improvement, indicating the potential of the curved-scintillator-based system for high-resolution inspection of cylindrical lithium-ion batteries.

title: Observing spatial photon dissipation in cellular light-energy reallocation
Programmed micromotors and nanomotors for active penetration of physiological barriers
abstract: Micro- and nanomotors (MNMs) represent a paradigm shift in active delivery systems, leveraging autonomous propulsion to overcome complex physiological barriers. A critical determinant of their success is structural programmability. This review systematically delineates how the nanoscale engineering of geometric asymmetry, surface bio-interfaces, and mechanical deformability governs the barrier-penetrating capabilities of MNMs. Rather than merely stating the importance of structure, we elucidate how programming these specific physicochemical attributes allows MNMs to efficiently convert diverse energy inputs (for example, enzymatic, magnetic, acoustic, and photothermal) into targeted local physical effects, such as localized shear stress, thermophoretic gradients, and cavitation forces. These programmable physical effects serve as the direct mechanisms for actively tearing through or navigating viscous mucus, high-shear vascular endothelia, dense tumor interstitium, and subcellular compartments. Furthermore, by evaluating comparative performance metrics across different structural designs and proposing prescriptive design principles, this review offers concrete mechanistic insights for engineering next-generation MNMs toward clinical translation.

title: Tracking bacterial active matter in complex environments using deep learning
abstract: Active matter refers to materials that consist of energy-harvesting sub-components that interact to give non-trivial sub- to super-diffusive properties. Tracking such components is challenging due to their variable size, shape, and density—especially in complex environments—making traditional, hand-tuned algorithms unreliable, which limits their generality. We address this by applying deep learning to perform single-particle tracking of bacterial active matter in environments with walls and obstructions by chaining two neural networks for simultaneous detection and trajectory linking that are subsequently analyzed using standard statistical techniques. Remarkably, our models require only a single training example to generalize, enabling the detection of near-bulk flow in densely interacting systems. This approach obtains data that bridge the gap between discrete and continuous descriptions of active matter. It allows for a scalable path to test established theories against experimental data and hence uncover the fundamental principles that drive collective behavior in active matter.

title: Switchable pathways for precise carboxylic acid modification in proteins and antibodies
abstract: Historically, organic chemistry has been biased toward irreversible transformations. However, they have struggled to meet the selectivity demands from recent biopharma growth. Here, we establish the potential of reversible reactions within a multi-equilibria system from a multicomponent reaction (MCR), offering three switchable pathways for selective carboxylate modification in proteins and antibodies. The classical Ugi reaction yields heterogeneous mixtures, lysine being a major competitor. To address this, we developed a four-component reaction to render a four-component product (4CR-4CP). The 4CR-4CP can be disrupted and switched to 4CR-2CP or 3CR-2CP (>36 examples). Pathway exclusivity and carboxylate selectivity remain intact even at >99% bioconjugation. The method enables single- or dual-site probe installation and E21-labeling of insulin without compromising receptor binding or downstream signaling. The strategy extends to monoclonal antibodies, generating carboxylate-selective antibody-fluorophore and drug conjugates (AFCs and ADCs) for antigen-specific labeling and antiproliferative activity, opening a unique platform for multi-equilibria driven protein modification.

title: High-synchronization wearable fNIRS-EEG system for investigating neurovascular coupling dynamics at millisecond temporal resolution
abstract: Here, we report a wearable functional near-infrared spectroscopy-electroencephalogram (fNIRS-EEG) system to overcome the temporal resolution mismatch between the two modalities, enabling precise investigation of neurovascular coupling dynamics (NVC). By implementing an orthogonal encoding and cyclic decoding scheme, the system achieves fNIRS acquisition at up to 1,000 Hz simultaneously with EEG, while maintaining high signal fidelity across 52 optical and 32 electrical channels. Systematic validation through phantom experiments, physiological tests, and auditory-evoked response measurements confirms the system's ability to concurrently capture fast neural activity and hemodynamic correlates. Feature-level correlation analysis further reveals strong links between optical neuronal signals and event-related potentials. This technological advance provides a powerful platform for studying rapid neuronal signals, with broad implications for cognitive neuroscience, clinical diagnostics, and brain-computer interfaces.

title: Late-stage C(sp3)-H cross-coupling for high-throughput access to bioactive peptides via Pd catalysis
abstract: Amide bond formations and Pd-catalyzed C–C cross-couplings are among the most frequently used chemical reactions in drug discovery. By chemically linking amino acids or (hetero)aromatics as diversified building blocks, these reactions generate vast combinatorial libraries of peptides and small molecules, respectively, for high-throughput testing in bioassays. While this strategy has proven highly successful in drug development, the pursuit of future drug candidates calls for convergent C(sp 3 ) cross-coupling catalysis that covers underexplored molecular space. Here, we report on the convergent, late-stage C–C cross-coupling between (hetero)aromatic drug scaffolds and N-terminal glycine residues in bioactive peptides. This enables the diversification of small-molecule scaffolds with short-chain peptides or, inversely, linking bioactive peptides with drug-like (hetero)aromatics. In addition, we show that the potential of this reaction further extends to solid-phase peptide synthesis and high-throughput library synthesis, key synthetic technologies in drug discovery.

title: Neck-head robotic architecture for dexterous, high-precision manipulation in unstructured environments
abstract: Soft continuum robots (SCRs) have attracted significant attention due to their intrinsic compliance, high adaptability, and safe interaction capability in unstructured scenarios. However, implementing high-precision manipulation, particularly the simultaneous and accurate control of positioning and orientation, remains a significant challenge. This study proposes a bio-inspired neck-head robotic architecture (BNH-RA) that leverages the environmental adaptability of the neck portion while incorporating the kinematic precision of the head portion. Then, a collaborative control framework based on the visual information separation strategy is developed, which enables decoupled yet coordinated regulation of positional and orientational motions. Moreover, the BNH-RA is mounted on a mobile platform to construct an inspection system, and experimental evaluations conducted in unmanned storage scenarios illustrate the system's ability to perform cargo inspection and high-precision marking tasks. These results underscore the potential of the BNH-RA for a wide range of robotic applications that require environmental adaptability and high-precision manipulation.

title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals contrasting retinal responses to graphene oxide and Ti3C2Tx MXene quantum dots
abstract: The burgeoning application of nanomaterials in biomedicine demands a rigorous definition of their biosafety profiles. Here, we report the ocular biocompatibility of graphene oxide quantum dots (GOQDs) and Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene QDs using the mouse eye, in vitro assays, and spatial transcriptomics. In vitro , both materials exhibit dose-dependent cytotoxicity, with GOQDs maintaining higher retinal cell viability. Intravitreal delivery in vivo demonstrates that GOQDs are well tolerated. Conversely, Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene QDs induce marked ocular pathology, including corneal edema, cataract formation, vitreous opacification, and retinal structural damage. Histopathological and spatial transcriptomics reveal that at elevated doses, Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene QDs are associated with retinal disorganization and reductions in photoreceptors, bipolar cells, and amacrine cells (ACs). Mechanistically, GOQDs trigger adaptive responses, whereas under higher concentration conditions, Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene QDs show enrichment of fibrosis, DNA damage, and microglial dysfunction. This comparison establishes a safety hierarchy between these zero-dimensional nanomaterials and provides a framework for designing safer nanotechnologies.

title: A data-driven framework for forecasting the spatial-temporal distribution of energy-use flows in air transportation
abstract: In the Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario, aviation electrification serves as a promising approach to improving energy efficiency and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. We present a data-driven protocol that forecasts the spatiotemporal distribution of energy-use flows across China's air transportation network. Using flight records aggregated monthly, we construct airport-level networks and generate scenario-specific energy-flow predictions with preference structures. We train and evaluate a multi-output machine learning framework of (1) classifiers for dual link prediction (addition, retention, and removal) and (2) regressors for weight (energy-demand) prediction, identifying suitable models for non-simultaneous, long-horizon forecasting. Results show that strengthened networks exhibit a bias toward rising energy demand, with hubs concentrating intensive flows, while non-hubs struggle to sustain links. This provides evidence for policies on electric plane deployment and airport-to-grid coordination.

title: Mechanobiological mechanisms of bacterial infection-host defense interactions
abstract: Recent advances in infection biology have increasingly underscored that mechanical forces and microenvironmental cues shape host-pathogen interactions in critical, stage-specific manners. Key mechanical inputs—such as fluid shear stress, cortical tension, and extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness—can markedly modulate bacterial adhesion to host cells, subsequent invasion, and dissemination. In this review, we propose a mechano-regulatory framework in which infection and host defense co-evolve through a bidirectional "mechanical tug-of-war." Within this framework, mechanical cues tune bacterial behaviors, while host tissues mount mechanically driven defenses, including epithelial extrusion, to remove infected cells. We further highlight emerging anti-infective opportunities that target mechanical vulnerabilities, ranging from force-stabilized adhesion inhibitors to engineered, mechanically gated therapeutics and stiffness-tailored implants. By integrating mechanobiology, mechanomedicine, and microbiology, this growing field may enable more targeted and effective therapies for bacterial infections.

title: Advancing wide-band-gap perovskite solar cells via vapor-phase deposition
abstract: Wide-band-gap perovskite solar cells (WBG PSCs) hold significant optoelectronic potential, with applications spanning building-integrated photovoltaics, large-area modules, and tandem solar cells. Vapor-phase deposition, leveraging its unique solvent-free processing, provides an ideal platform to address critical WBG perovskite challenges, including halide segregation, phase instability, and defect control. This review critically assesses the vapor-phase technology landscape for WBG perovskites. It first dissects fundamental physicochemical challenges in vacuum environments: mixed-halide lattice thermodynamic metastability, precursor sublimation kinetic mismatch, and complex organic cation volatility. It then systematically evaluates advanced deposition methodologies, ranging from sequential evaporation to hybrid vapor-solution routes, alongside optimization strategies spanning nucleation thermodynamics, bulk defect management, and interface energy alignment. It further examines the translation of material innovations into functional devices, highlighting vapor deposition's advantages in semitransparent cells, scalable modules, and high-efficiency perovskite/silicon tandem cells, before outlining key challenges and future directions to guide both fundamental research and industrial-scale development.

title: Vapor condensation enhancement in passive solar water harvesting
abstract: Passive solar water harvesting technologies, including solar distillation and sorption-based atmospheric water harvesting, are important for addressing the ever-increasing global freshwater shortage due to their unique feasibility in all regions. While substantial advancements in vapor generation have been achieved recently, condensation in passive solar water harvesting systems remains the final step for freshwater production. However, compared to the advanced condensation design adopted in other technologies, such as fog collectors and heat pipes, condensation enhancement has lagged behind in passive solar water harvesting, resulting in a discrepancy of nearly 35% between vapor generation and water collection. In this review, the condensation process in passive solar water harvesting systems is systematically analyzed in three stages (i.e., vapor diffusion, droplet nucleation, and passive water transport and collection). We begin with the theoretical analysis of the passive solar water harvesting process, identifying the challenges in condensation enhancement. Subsequently, we summarize and compare the condensation designs adopted in both existing passive solar water harvesting technologies and other disciplines such as heat pipes and fog collectors, evaluating the feasibility of these strategies in passive solar water harvesting. With the above analyses, we conclude with the future opportunities of condensation enhancement in passive solar water harvesting, which could supplement the missing half for developing high-performance passive solar water harvesting technologies in the future.

title: Photoinduced Cu-catalyzed chemo- and stereoselective histidine modification
abstract: Late-Stage-Functionalization (LSF) of peptides and proteins represents a challenge of reaction design as well as the most facile route to various and abundant conjugates. Due to the presence of multiple reactive sites on polypeptide molecules, achieving chemically and stereoselective modifications poses a significant challenge. Herein, we report the highly chemo- and stereoselective modification of histidine-containing peptides via a photoinduced Cu-catalyzed 1,2-bifunctionalization reaction of alkynes. This reaction exhibits remarkable stereoselectivity (Z/E) and chemo-selectivity, specifically targeting the nitrogen atom at N-1 position of the histidine imidazole ring. Under exceedingly mild reaction conditions, the late-stage diversification of structurally complex peptides, radical precursors, and alkynes with high yields and selectivity. Its utility has been demonstrated in a series of important peptide drugs and complex natural products. Therefore, our technique is a versatile and powerful tool for late-stage orthogonal bioconjugation. Moreover, the batch and flow protocol described herein can be applied to obtain a broad series of alkenylated histidine-containing polypeptides.

title: Efficient co-programming of intercellular mechanics and signaling for complex developmental patterns
abstract: Intercellular ligand-receptor signaling is fundamental for producing diverse cell types and complex developmental patterns, yet design principles—particularly regarding timing, spatial structure, cell lineage, and molecular resource—remain unclear. With public literature and data, we outline the cell-cell contact maps and signaling during embryogenesis in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans . We devise a multi-phase field model incorporating crosstalk and memory to simulate how neighboring cells interact through mechanics and signaling, driving complex developmental patterns with diverse cell types. Our model reproduces the 1- to 12-cell-stage spatial structures and demonstrates the C. elegans program's efficiency in enhancing pattern complexity. While signaling-regulated cell-division directions ensure fidelity of spatial structures and signaling, the resultant patterns prove robust against variations in cell-division timing and noise in cell movement and adhesion. Finally, we develop an optimization algorithm to automatically design signaling programs on top of mechanical architectures, exemplified by C. elegans embryos and synNotch spheroids.

title: Precise direct patterning of metal-organic frameworks: Chemical mechanisms, strategies, and applications
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are emergent materials for photonic, electronic, and sensing applications, creating an urgent demand for patterning methods that bridge their structural and chemical tunability to high-performance integrated devices. Conventional top-down and bottom-up approaches are constrained by resist contamination, limited compatibility, and insufficient resolution. Direct patterning techniques provide distinct advantages, including higher resolution, resist-free processing, broad compatibility across MOF chemistries, and the ability to preserve crystallinity and porosity. This review consolidates recent advances in direct MOF patterning, elucidates the chemical and mechanistic principles that govern each strategy, and evaluates their advantages and limitations in terms of resolution, roughness, and structural integrity. By integrating material design with process optimization, we highlight the key factors that enable high-fidelity MOF patterning and assess their emerging applications in photonics, electronics, and sensing. We also outline the major challenges that remain and identify opportunities for advancing next-generation direct patterning of MOFs.

title: A universal deep learning framework for digital PCR and ELISA
abstract: Image-processing frameworks are critical for the absolute quantification of nucleic acids and proteins, in which accurate analysis of microreactors generated by digital PCR or digital ELISA is required. However, existing methods often suffer from reduced accuracy at high microreactor densities and limited generalizability. Here, we propose Microreactor-Vision, a deep learning framework that integrates an enhanced U-Net-based segmentation model with a lightweight convolutional neural network classifier. The framework achieves >99% quantitative accuracy and has been validated across multiple fluorescence channels and diverse microreactor architectures. Microreactor-Vision further demonstrates an ultra-low limit of detection and a broad dynamic range (10 −1 –10 4 copies/μL), with strong linearity between predicted and actual concentrations (coefficient of determination [R 2 ] > 0.99). To our knowledge, it achieves the highest detection throughput and accuracy reported to date while maintaining efficient inference speed. Microreactor-Vision offers a rapid, cost-effective, and robust solution for AI-driven absolute quantification, supporting translational and clinical biosensing applications.

title: A multi-agent AI framework for explainable battery system maintenance
abstract: The operation and maintenance (O&M) of battery energy-storage systems (BESSs) remain dominated by reactive, expert-dependent diagnostics. Although cell-level inconsistencies can provide early warning signals of degradation and safety risks, the lack of scalable and interpretable decision-support frameworks prevents these signals from being effectively translated into operational actions. Here, we introduce an inconsistency-driven O&M paradigm for large-scale BESSs that systematically transforms routine monitoring data into explainable and decision-oriented guidance via large language model-based semantic reasoning. Using 8 months of field data from an in-service BESS comprising 3,564 cells, we demonstrate how real-world O&M queries are converted into actionable maintenance insights, reducing response time and operational cost by over 80% compared with conventional expert-driven practices. These results establish a scalable pathway for intelligent O&M of BESSs, with direct implications for reliability and cost-effective integration of energy storage into modern power systems.

title: Hydrogel-based dynamic structural colors for dual-mode image encryption
abstract: Overcoming the complexity of multi-mode optical encryption, this work demonstrates a simple approach for dual-mode image encryption that employs configurable hydrogel nanograting arrays, enabling a dynamically tunable structural color. Hydrogel nanograting arrays were fabricated on an aluminum layer, supporting the coupling of surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) with polarization selectivity for the first-mode encryption. The resonance of SPPs was configurable with periodicity; the coloration was stepwise tunable with the swelling/deswelling of hydrogel nanogratings in response to environmental humidity. Furthermore, a second exposure method is developed to selectively modify the swellability of the hydrogel structures, inducing a second-mode encryption based on distinct humidity-responsive color changes. The self-driven tunability, real-time adjustability, repeatability, and long-term stability of this hydrogel-based dynamic structural color engineer its efficient applications in multispectral camouflage, optical information security, and intelligent anti-counterfeit.

title: Tailoring mechanical properties of hydrogels for wound repair from perspectives of simulating cellular microenvironment
abstract: Wound repair remains a major challenge in clinical practice. Wounds are often characterized by abnormal stiffness, altered viscoelasticity, and abnormal tension, which can impair cellular repair functions. While hydrogels are promising candidates due to their biocompatibility and tunable properties, conventional designs often function as passive barriers, lacking the capacity to actively correct the hostile mechanical microenvironment. Consequently, there is a pressing need to develop hydrogels that not only retain their excellent biocompatibility but also actively restore physiological mechanical cues. This review summarizes strategies for regulating the mechanical properties of hydrogels and explores the molecular mechanisms through which mechanical changes in wounds influence the repair process. It further discusses the design principles of various types of mechanically biomimetic hydrogels developed in recent years, along with their therapeutic applications in treating challenging wounds such as deep tissue injuries and diabetic ulcers. Through a systematic analysis of hydrogel mechanical design strategies and their underlying mechanisms, this article aims to offer a comprehensive framework and specific design principles to guide the development of next-generation mechanically biomimetic hydrogels for wound-healing applications.

title: Cryogenic microwave mixing and phase control in superconducting quantum paraelectric resonator
abstract: Scaling quantum processors requires cryogenic microwave components to minimize thermal load and wiring complexity. However, conventional microwave components such as mixers and phase shifters perform poorly at millikelvin temperatures. Here, we report an SrTiO 3 (STO)-based microwave frequency mixer and phase shifter operating at sub-Kelvin temperatures. Utilizing the effective χ (2) nonlinearity of STO in the quantum paraelectric state, induced by a static or oscillating field, we achieve efficient microwave frequency mixing. Our device features an aluminum superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator on STO, which resonantly enhances mixing characteristics. The exceptionally high field-tunable dielectric constant of STO—approximately 30,000—allows for highly compact architectures and facilitates voltage-controlled phase shifting. Furthermore, we demonstrate multi-tone frequency mixing via phase modulation, facilitating spectral filtering and shaping. These STO-based devices provide a transformative approach to the generation of intricate microwave waveforms, tailoring control and readout signals in multi-qubit systems and paving the way for co-located quantum-classical integration.

title: Self-powered piezoelectric nanocomposite films for wearable health-signal monitoring
abstract: With the growing demand for flexible electronics in health monitoring, the development of sensing materials that combine environmental sustainability, biocompatibility, and high piezoelectric performance has become a major research focus. Here, we report a barium titanate (BaTiO 3 [BT])/hydroxyapatite (Ca 10 (PO 4 ) 6 (OH) 2 [HA])/polylactic acid (PLA) nanocomposite film fabricated via spin coating, exhibiting enhanced piezoelectric performance and durability. At a BT/HA content of 5 wt %, the composite film achieves an open-circuit voltage ( V oc ) of 8.56 V, a short-circuit current ( I sc ) of 185 nA, and a piezoelectric coefficient ( d 33 ) of 2.9 pC/N, representing a significant improvement over the pure PLA. The film also demonstrates excellent cyclic stability over 3,000 s under 20 N at 1 Hz and favorable cytocompatibility. Simulations reveal that the optimized composition shows more uniform surface potential, stress, and electric field distribution, consistent with experimental observation. Furthermore, the film enables sensitive detection of various human motions. This work provides an effective strategy for designing sustainable, self-powered flexible sensors for health-monitoring applications.

title: Data-driven molecular design rules for electrolytes in CO2 electroreduction
abstract: CO 2 electroreduction offers a promising route to convert CO 2 into valuable chemicals and fuels. CO 2 electroreduction research has predominantly focused on catalyst innovation, yet the electrolyte, equally critical for governing CO 2 solubility and ion transport, remains comparatively underexplored. Here, we introduce a multiscale informatics framework integrating density functional theory, conductor-like screening model for realistic solvents (COSMO-RS) thermodynamics, molecular dynamics (MD), and machine learning to accelerate electrolyte discovery. The framework focuses on bulk-phase electrolyte properties that govern solvent stability, CO 2 solubility, and transport, and thus electrolyte performance in CO 2 electroreduction. Hierarchical screening of 1.3 million organic molecules identified six high-performing candidates, validated through MD simulations, and benchmarked against twenty experimentally tested electrolytes. All data, descriptors, and pretrained models are consolidated in the open-access COSMIC (CO 2 solvent materials informatics collection) database. Our analysis reveals how molecular polarity, protic character, and electronic structure govern CO 2 solubility and viscosity, providing transferable molecular design rules for next-generation CO 2 electroreduction electrolytes.

title: Multiplier benefits of integrating household-scale water-efficient sanitation technologies with centralized water resource-recovery facilities
abstract: Conventional sewer-based wastewater treatment systems are capital- and energy-intensive, with limited flexibility to accommodate climate and demographic change. While household-scale water-efficient sanitation technologies (WEST) are increasingly deployed to address access and equity challenges, their broader systemic impacts remain largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that integrating WEST, especially household reinvented toilets (HRT) that process both grey- and black water (gb-HRT), with existing sewered water resource recovery facilities (WRRFs) unlocks substantial and synergistic reductions in energy consumption, and operating costs. Further system optimization significantly improves both energy and monetary savings across all WEST-WRRF combinations and coverage levels. Our findings reveal a systems-level opportunity to reconfigure sanitation infrastructure for resilience, circularity, and equity, not by expanding centralized treatment, but by leveraging household interventions as infrastructural leverage points in the global sanitation-energy nexus.

title: Decisive role of pore-edge termination in determining the CO2 selectivity of Å-scale pores in graphene
abstract: Zero-dimensional pores in graphene hold strong promise for carbon capture, yet the role of pore-edge functional groups remains poorly understood. Using molecular dynamics simulations and potential-of-mean-force calculations, we show that pore-edge chemistry determines whether Å-scale pores are selective. Oxygen-functionalized pores (O-pores) exhibit highly selective CO 2 /O 2 transport, whereas similarly sized hydrogen-terminated pores (H-pores) are non-selective. This difference arises from markedly stronger CO 2 -pore interactions in O-pores, where CO 2 adsorbs at the pore mouth for up to a nanosecond, compared to residence times up to two orders of magnitude shorter in H-pores. We further develop a velocity-corrected transition-state-theory model that accurately predicts gas transport through both pore types by accounting for molecule-pore interactions at the transition state. These findings provide a robust framework for rational membrane design and highlight the benefits of oxidative pore-formation protocols for carbon-capture membranes.

title: Transforming urban energy systems with scalable non-invasive building thermal sensing
abstract: The urgent need for sustainable buildings has accelerated the development of non-invasive sensing methods to assess thermal parameters, such as thermal transmittance, temperature, and humidity. Unlike intrusive traditional approaches that lack scalability, non-invasive techniques, including infrared thermography and ground-penetrating radar, offer contactless diagnostics. However, their transition into robust sensing systems is hindered by environmental sensitivity, a lack of standardization, and limited capacity to capture large-scale indoor-outdoor interactions. This review systematically analyzes these barriers and presents emerging integrated solutions. Key advancements include unmanned aerial vehicle multimodal sensing that enables high-throughput data collection and physics-informed learning frameworks that enhance measurement accuracy and model interoperability. These approaches can transform these techniques from isolated diagnostic tools into scalable urban-level intelligence systems. This transformation fundamentally strengthens building energy modeling at the city scale, providing critical data support for decarbonization pathways and climate-resilient urban planning.

title: Elastohydrodynamic mechanisms govern beat pattern transitions in eukaryotic flagella
abstract: Abstract Eukaryotic cilia and flagella exhibit complex beating patterns that change depending on environmental conditions such as fluid viscosity. The mechanism behind these beat pattern transitions remains unclear, although they are thought to arise from changes in the internal forcing provided by the axoneme. We show here that such transitions may arise universally across species via an elastohydrodynamic mechanism. We perform simulations of inextensible and unshearable but twistable Kirchhoff rods driven internally by a travelling bending-moment wave in a fixed plane in the material frame of the rods. We show that, for a large range of beating amplitudes and frequencies, the internally planar driving wave results in the growth of twist perturbations. Outside this domain, the driving leads to simple planar waveforms. Within the non-planar domain, we observe quasiplanar, helical, and complex – perhaps chaotic – beating patterns. The transitions between these states depend quantitatively on physical parameters such as the internal forcing, flagellum stiffness and length, viscosity of the ambient medium, or the presence of a plane wall. Beat pattern transitions in our simulations can be mapped to similar transitions observed in bull and sea urchin sperm when the medium viscosity is varied. Comparison of the simulation results with experimentally observed transitional viscosities in our experiments and elsewhere suggests an assay whereby one can estimate the average force exerted by dynein motors. This could potentially lead to diagnostic assays measuring the health of sperm based on their beating pattern. Significance Statement The ability of flagella and cilia to manipulate their beating waveforms in different physical environments has important implications for human and animal health. Beat transitions in mammalian sperm flagella, for example, may help sperm navigate the complex reproductive tract to reach the egg. Abnormal beating behaviour, which may have a range of unknown underlying causes, can result in ciliopathies and reproductive disorders. This work provides insight into the physical origins of beat transitions in flagella and shows how they depend quantitatively on flagellum stiffness and length, internal driving provided by the axoneme, viscosity of the ambient medium, and the presence of a plane wall. This could allow one to diagnose the root cause of an abnormal flagellar beat and thus design appropriate treatment.

title: Pyridinyl ring defines a noncanonical P1-S1 axis that revamps inhibitor design against coronaviral main proteases
abstract: The coronaviral main protease (M pro ), cleaving viral polyproteins at an invariant glutamine (Gln) P1 residue through canonical recognition by its S1 pocket, is a mature target for antiviral development. However, how P1-S1 interactions involving chemical entities beyond Gln or its derivatives impact inhibitor design remains obscure. Here we report a noncanonical P1-S1 axis formed between the S1 pocket and a pyridinyl P1, further expanded by occupying an oxyanion hole within the S1 pocket, enabling design of high-potency non-covalent inhibitors. This axis is illustrated by X-ray crystallography-yielding cocrystal structures of M pro from SARS-CoV-1, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV complexed with our inhibitors. Importantly, a covalent peptidyl inhibitor bearing an isoquinoline ring (a pyridinyl derivative) at P1 is ∼1,000-fold stronger than nirmatrelvir against SARS-CoV-2 in vitro and comparable, as a monotherapy, to Paxlovid in reducing infection in vivo . Our findings redefine protease-inhibitor recognition and provide a blueprint for designing next-generation M pro inhibitors.

title: Platelet-membrane-coated photosynthetic oxygen production system for diabetic wound repair
abstract: Oxygen is essential for cellular metabolism and bioenergy production, and insufficient oxygen supply is a hallmark of multiple pathological conditions, including diabetic foot ulcers and impaired wound healing. Persistent hypoxia severely compromises tissue regeneration, making these wounds particularly difficult to treat. Here, we developed platelet-membrane (PM)-coated nanothylakoid units (NTU@PMs) for targeted oxygen delivery to hypoxic cells, particularly macrophages involved in wound repair. Under light illumination, NTU@PMs efficiently generated oxygen, alleviated macrophage hypoxia, reprogrammed macrophage metabolism, and promoted macrophage migration and phagocytosis. In diabetic wound and flap mouse models, NTU@PMs alleviated wound hypoxia and accelerated tissue repair. These findings identify NTU@PMs as a promising strategy for the treatment of diabetic wounds and potentially other hypoxia-associated disorders.

title: Production of extracellular vesicles from beta cells in stirred tanks enhances maturation and ectosome release with preserved immune properties
abstract: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) derived from beta cells are promising therapeutics for diabetes through their ability to modulate inflammation, preserve pancreatic function, and limit pathogenic mechanisms. For clinical translation, scalable production in a stirred tank bioreactor (STR) is essential, but shear stress can affect sEV function. Here, we report the influence of culture mode, medium formulation, and process parameters on beta cell performance and sEV quality. Small spheroid culture promotes beta cell maturation without affecting sEV yield, whereas stirring increases cellular stress and decreases viability. An optimized three-step bioprocess maximizes cell viability and sEV yields at high cell density in STR over short production periods. The produced sEVs display high purity, preserved membrane integrity, and immunomodulatory activity by reducing T-lymphocyte proliferation and IFN-γ cytokine secretion in an allogenic mixed lymphocyte reaction. Flow cytometry shows enhanced ectosome production in STR, and low glucose medium promotes insulin sorting into beta cell-derived sEVs.

title: Crystallization as a local symmetry-breaking event in a tunable soft matter
abstract: Crystallization represents a pivotal local symmetry-breaking process that fundamentally shapes the structural and functional properties of material systems. Despite its importance, direct observation of its earliest stages remains elusive. Here, we introduce an in situ cryo-crystallization approach that captures the nucleation dynamics within a tunable soft-matter field composed of oxometalate assemblies. Employing a dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO)-water glass matrix, we finely control the solvent environment to suppress background noise and inhibit mechanical fracture, thereby enabling unprecedented visualization of symmetry breaking at the onset of crystallization. This method reveals the formation of ordered oxometalate domains that precede the crystallization of {Mo 7 } clusters, offering rare insights into pre-nucleation ordering. Our findings establish a framework for interpreting crystallization as a symmetry-breaking process and provide a new strategy to engineer material architectures through controlled phase evolution.

title: Scientific AI systems require domain-aware robustness validation
