abstract: AI has become an essential tool in many areas of scientific discovery. However, its robustness, particularly in high-stakes scientific applications, remains insufficiently understood. While adversarial vulnerabilities have been widely studied in image recognition, their implications in scientific disciplines, where physical constraints and numerical stability are critical, have not been thoroughly explored. This work presents a systematic evaluation of AI model fragility across five scientific domains: climate modeling, quantum chemistry, fluid dynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and wireless communications. We demonstrate that small, structured perturbations can destabilize predictions in all of these domains, even in models that achieve high accuracy under normal conditions. Furthermore, the failure patterns vary across domains, suggesting that these vulnerabilities are domain specific. Our findings underscore the importance of assessing AI robustness in scientific contexts and offer preliminary insights into how to design more resilient and reliable AI systems for scientific applications.

title: Pt-based catalyst degradation in membrane electrode assemblies for polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells
abstract: This review focuses on understanding catalyst degradation within membrane electrode assembly (MEA) of polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). The review provides an overview of mechanisms and pathways for Pt and Pt-alloy degradation as well as associated carbon corrosion within the MEAs and explains methods for quantifying it within the PEMFC assembly. Local environment and operating conditions have a large impact on water and heat management and hence impact Pt dissolution and redeposition, as well as alloying element dissolution. Advanced operando techniques are overviewed to characterize this heterogeneous degradation of catalysts within the complex operating environment of fuel cells. Mitigation strategies are presented, focusing on catalyst design through Pt particle size and morphology optimization, interface engineering, and optimization of MEA components to improve catalyst durability and fuel cell performance. The outlook and future directions are presented at the end.

title: Independent switching of interfacial exchange bias via antiferromagnet-mediated spin-orbit torque
abstract: Electrical control of exchange bias in spintronic heterostructures typically relies on magnetic field cooling, ferromagnet reversal, or metallic antiferromagnets. Here, we report the simultaneous electrical switching of exchange bias and longitudinal resistance via pulse currents in a Pt/NiO/NiFe heterostructure. The switching direction of interfacial pinned spins is independent of the NiFe layer's magnetization, contrasting with ferromagnet-governed scenarios. By systematically excluding thermal and Oersted-field effects, we attribute this behavior to the reversal of interfacial pinned spins driven by spin-orbit torque mediated through the antiferromagnetic insulator NiO. Supported by spin Hall magnetoresistance measurements and macro-spin simulations, these results demonstrate an insulator-mediated switching mechanism that operates without ferromagnet reversal or charge transport through the antiferromagnet. This work provides a platform for investigating interfacial spin dynamics in antiferromagnetic insulator-based heterostructures.

title: Mechanically programmable metasurface for ultralow-power subterahertz beam steering
abstract: Metasurfaces are promising for shaping terahertz wavefronts, but reconfigurable platforms remain constrained by trade-offs among programmability, energy consumption, and cost. Many active metasurfaces require continuous electrical bias to hold states, whereas low-cost passive designs are static. Here, we report a mechanically latched programmable metasurface that steers subterahertz beams by tuning the period of periodic wavy metal elements, thereby reconfiguring the diffraction-induced phase distribution. A lead-screw-driven scissor-telescopic mechanism provides repeatable millimeter-scale geometric tuning under microcontroller control and retains states without holding power. Experiments over 110–170 GHz demonstrate continuous beam steering with a 1.2° average pointing error, simultaneous steering of up to five beams, and real-time tracking up to 25°/s. In a 150-GHz 16-quadrature amplitude modulation (16-QAM) link, it supports multi-direction reception with symbol error rates below 10 −6 in target beam directions. With a US$21.12 prototype cost and microwatt-level standby electronics power, this metasurface offers a low-cost route to energy-efficient beamforming for dense, mobile subterahertz links.

title: Acoustomagneto-electrocatalytic oxygen evolution reaction enhancement
abstract: Green hydrogen production is constrained by the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Here, we show that coupling an acoustomagneto-electrocatalytic (AME) effect to a ferromagnetic Ni catalyst yields an order-of-magnitude enhancement in OER activity. Nanometer-amplitude electromechanical vibrations on a piezoelectric chip induce local magnetic fields at the catalyst interface, increasing magnetization and dynamically reconfiguring magnetic domains—without the need for permanent magnets. Magnetic force microscopy and nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry reveal enlarged domains that reduce spin disorder and expose more catalytically active sites. This low-energy, dynamic approach lowers the OER overpotential by 0.34 V at 20 mA cm −2 via the synergistic coupling between induced magnetization, strain, and enhanced convective transport, collectively outperforming what can be achieved by these individual effects alone or in combination. The AME coupling thus provides a non-chemical, externally addressable route to exploit the intrinsic magnetoelastic properties of catalysts, with broad implications for their application across spin-dependent electrocatalytic processes.

title: Stratum corneum lipids in a hydration gradient exhibit robust lamellar organization and responsive fluidity
abstract: The outermost skin layer, the stratum corneum (SC), forms a responsive barrier where molecular transport depends on the structure and dynamics of its extracellular lipid matrix. SC lipids predominantly adopt a long-periodicity lamellar (LPP) phase across a wide hydration range, but how this structural resilience relates to the strong hydration dependence of skin permeability remains unclear. It is also not well understood how bulk observations translate to physiological conditions, where the SC is present in a steep water gradient. Here, we characterize SC lipids under both bulk and non-equilibrium conditions induced by a hydration gradient. In bulk, lipids form a largely solid LPP structure. Increasing hydration leads to increased lipid mobility without disrupting LPP structure. Under a hydration gradient, lipids assemble into oriented multilayers parallel to the interface towards air. These findings support a model in which SC lipids buffer humidity through hydration-controlled modulation of fluidity while preserving a robust lamellar scaffold, linking structure to transport in the SC.

title: Structurally defined mRNA-LNPs formulation using automated inline monitoring and hydrodynamically enhanced system
abstract: The clinical translation efficacy of mRNA-loaded lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) critically depends on their structural and compositional uniformity, but conventional batch-to-batch processing methods struggle to meet this challenge. To address this, we developed a closed-loop robotic platform integrating a computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-optimized microfluidic mixer with asymmetric herringbone grooves and an inline organic electrochemical transistor (OECT) for real-time impedance monitoring. The mixer achieved >99.99% mixing efficiency at flow rates ≥ 10 mL/min with minimal energy dissipation, and this accomplishment enabled rapid synthesis of monodisperse LNPs (polydispersity index [PDI] < 0.1 and encapsulation efficiency > 95%). Coupled with real-time OECT-based feedback for detecting compositional changes, the system produced LNPs with superior structural homogeneity, a higher mRNA payload, and a lower empty particle ratio—which are key clinical side effects of mRNA-LNPs—compared with a leading commercial product. In vivo results confirmed enhanced transfection efficiency, thus directly linking optimized hydrodynamic control to improved functional performance and underscoring the platform's potential for scalable, high-quality LNPs production.

title: Microelectrodes enable dynamic biointerfaces for closed-loop organs-on-chips
abstract: Organs-on-chips (OoCs) have emerged as a revolutionary toolbox to replicate the in vivo microenvironment and simulate the key functions of human tissues and organs. These systems offer a promising alternative to animal models in disease modeling, drug screening, and personalized medicine. A key limitation of conventional OoCs, however, is their inability to capture and respond to bioelectrical signals, hindering elucidation of dynamic (patho)physiological processes. Moreover, most OoCs with integrated microelectrode sensors operate in an open-loop configuration, lacking actuation mechanisms to modulate these processes guided by real-time monitoring and biofeedback. Herein, we explore the diverse applications of integrated microelectrode sensors within OoCs and identify both technical challenges and emerging opportunities. We discuss the state-of-the-art progress in electrode materials and sensor designs that enable the closed-loop framework in OoC systems, thus creating real-time sensing/monitoring, stimulation, and therapeutic interventions. These closed-loop systems promise to unlock new possibilities in adaptive drug delivery, responsive tissue engineering, and precision medicine. Ultimately, we emphasize that a holistic, system-level design approach, rather than a sole focus on electrode performance, is crucial to advancing the next generation of microelectrode-integrated closed-loop OoCs.

title: RuC-Cu nanoparticles on laser-induced N,P-doped graphene for cost-effective and synergistic-catalytic alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: Developing efficient and cost-effective electrocatalysts for alkaline hydrogen evolution (HER) to replace expensive Pt-based catalysts remains a critical challenge. Herein, we report a strategically designed catalyst by anchoring adjacent Cu and RuC nanoparticles on laser-induced N,P-doped graphene (RuC-Cu/NP-G). This catalyst operates via a synergistic process, whereby RuC serves as the primary active site with the adjacent Cu-mediated water dissociation. The RuC-Cu/NP-G catalyst demonstrates superior cost-effectiveness, with a mass activity 15 times higher and a price activity about 22 times greater than the commercial Pt/C catalyst. Moreover, the RuC-Cu/NP-G deposited on a carbon paper substrate can be directly used as the cathode in an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, delivering stable operation at high current densities up to 500 mA cm −2 for over 200 h. This work provides a rational design principle for high-performance, cost-efficient catalysts, highlighting a direct path toward scalable green hydrogen production.

title: Layer-by-layer polymeric films for buccal GLP-1 delivery
abstract: ABSTRACT Buccal delivery offers a promising alternative to oral drug administration by enabling direct systemic absorption and avoiding first-pass metabolism. Multilayer polymeric films represent a promising strategy for the sequential delivery of drug and absorption enhancer in the oral cavity. Here, dual- and triple-layer films were fabricated via slot-die coating, incorporating a GLP-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1-RA) and the penetration enhancer sodium glycodeoxycholate (GDC). These were co-loaded in dual-layer films or compartmentalized in triple-layer films. Scanning electron microscopy and optical coherence tomography confirmed well-defined, distinct layers with thicknesses suitable for buccal administration (339 ± 10.24 µm and 487 ± 36.5 µm for dual- and triple-layer films, respectively). Both designs exhibited good mucoadhesion and mucosal compatibility, and preserved the secondary structure of GLP-1-RA. In vitro release studies showed rapid diffusion of GDC and GLP-1-RA from dual-layer films, whereas triple-layer films enabled sustained, sequential release of GDC and GLP-1-RA. Ex vivo porcine buccal mucosa studies showed higher GLP-1-RA and GDC flux from triple-layer films compared to dual-layer films. The films also did not compromise epithelial integrity, in contrast to the direct application of GLP-1-RA and GDC, which caused significant epithelial disruption. These results demonstrate that multilayer film architecture and spatial layering can be harnessed to control release kinetics, maximize peptide penetration, and minimize tissue stress, offering a versatile platform for safe and effective peptide delivery. title: High transmittance retention in Ce-free glass for space solar panels
Ultrafast exciton-polaron dynamics in 2D Ruddlesden-Popper lead-halide perovskites
abstract: Two-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper (2D RP) hybrid perovskites exhibit enhanced chemical and structural stability compared with three-dimensional (3D) counterparts, making them attractive for optoelectronic applications. However, a quantitative understanding of coupled free-exciton (FE) and exciton-polaron (EP) dynamics in strict monolayer ( n = 1) RP perovskites remains limited. Here, we report a systematic investigation of FE-EP branching, interconversion, and interactions in monolayer 2D RP perovskites using femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy. Thin films with different organic spacers and fabrication routes are comparatively analyzed. We find EP binding energies of 50–65 meV in (BA) 2 PbI 4 and 37–39 meV in (PEA) 2 PbI 4 , together with a kinetic FE-EP balance persisting for tens of picoseconds. Films fabricated by the newly developed route exhibit weaker Auger annihilation and reduced hot-phonon bottlenecks, consistent with fewer traps and impurities. Rate-equation modeling quantitatively reproduces the coupled ultrafast dynamics.

title: Geometry-constrained prediction of catalytically competent kinase domains across the human kinome
abstract: Accurate structural modeling of kinases across functional states helps to understand signaling networks. However, most human kinases lack experimentally determined active-state structures, and existing computational methods often fail to predict catalytically competent conformations. Here, we present a geometry-constrained modeling framework based on AFEXplorer (AFEX) that enables robust prediction of active, ATP- and magnesium-bound states for 436 catalytic kinase domains across the human kinome. By explicitly enforcing biophysical criteria, AFEX overcomes the template dependence and conformational bias inherent in AlphaFold2 and AlphaFold3. Benchmarking against 156 kinase-substrate complexes shows that AFEX achieves a sub-2 Å backbone root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) in 99% of cases and accurately recapitulates critical catalytic features with precise ATP coordination. Notably, AFEX correctly predicted active conformations for epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2), whereas AlphaFold3 failed. These improvements are consistent across kinase families, including both well-characterized kinases and those underrepresented in AlphaFold's training data. AFEX provides a generalizable framework for studying active conformations and dynamics in kinases.

title: Interpretable neural operators enable topology-optimized cooling for concentrating photovoltaics
abstract: Concentrating photovoltaic systems generate high electrical output but also severe heat loads that reduce efficiency and reliability. Here, we report an interpretable neural operator framework for designing topology-optimized cooling channels for concentrating photovoltaics. A deep operator network learns the mapping from variable-depth flow field geometries to temperature and pressure fields, enabling rapid design screening while reducing computational energy use by more than 99% compared with conventional computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The optimized topology is fabricated by high-resolution stereolithography and tested under concentrated illumination. It lowers peak surface temperature from about 60°C to 54°C at 10 suns and is supported by numerical results showing a 15.7% increase in Nusselt number. Physical interpretation shows that topological undulations induce wall-normal secondary flows and improve field synergy, actively disrupting the thermal boundary layer. This framework provides a general route for interpretable, data-driven thermal fluid design in high-heat-flux energy devices.

title: A high-frequency, interaction-induced pneumatic oscillator enabling versatile soft robotics
abstract: Here, we report a high-frequency, interaction-induced pneumatic oscillator (HIPO) that generates self-sustained oscillations through internal mechanical-fluidic coupling in soft materials. Under constant airflow, reversible contact switching between a holed membrane and a flexible cover enables periodic oscillations up to 97 Hz without rigid valves or electronic control. The oscillator directly converts pneumatic energy into mechanical motion and drives diverse bioinspired soft robots, including crawling, flapping, and swimming systems. By integrating oscillation generation, actuation, and environmental interaction within a single compliant structure, HIPO establishes a compact and scalable approach to embodied actuation in soft robotics.

title: Radiation-tolerant GaAs heterojunction solar cells
abstract: A major challenge for space solar cells is degradation caused by high-energy radiation. This study aims to mitigate radiation degradation in GaAs solar cells by employing a hetero p-n junction. Our first approach focuses on reducing the radiation damage coefficient for carrier lifetime in the depletion region ( K τ d e p ). We demonstrate, through simulations and experiments, that forming the depletion region within the wide-bandgap emitter effectively reduces K τ d e p . Second, we seek to enhance the internal luminescence efficiency in the neutral region by increasing the doping concentration of the narrow-bandgap base layer. Simulations and experiments reveal that a high base doping concentration suppresses non-radiative recombination losses in the neutral region caused by radiation-induced defects. As a result, a thin-film GaAs heterojunction solar cell incorporating these two strategies achieves a maximum power point remaining factor of more than 99% after irradiation with 1 MeV electrons at a fluence of 1×10 14 cm −2 .

title: A supervised learning pipeline for decoding nanoparticle antibacterial activity
abstract: Antibacterial nanoparticles have significant promise for combating antimicrobial resistance, but their activity is governed by complex interactions between physicochemical properties and bacterial characteristics. Single-parameter studies therefore provide limited guidance for rational nanoparticle design. Here, we report a supervised machine learning framework for decoding nanoparticle antibacterial activity through parameter selection and predictive modeling. We curated datasets from 98 peer-reviewed studies containing experimentally validated minimum inhibitory concentration and minimum bactericidal concentration values. Physicochemical descriptors, including size, shape, surface charge, and synthesis route, were integrated with bacterial characteristics, including Gram stain, morphology, and oxygen requirement, to train regression and classification models. XGBoost and random forest achieved the strongest performance, with R² values of 0.91 and 0.92 for minimum inhibitory concentration prediction and 0.82 and 0.80 for minimum bactericidal concentration prediction, respectively. XGBoost also achieved a classification accuracy of 0.79. Feature analysis identified nanoparticle size, shape, synthesis method, Gram type, and oxygen requirement as key determinants of antibacterial efficacy.

title: Progress in electrochemical methane oxidation from catalyst to reactor scale
abstract: Electrochemical methane oxidation offers a promising route for converting methane into value-added oxygenates under ambient conditions, leveraging low-carbon electricity. Unlike traditional methods such as steam re-forming, ambient electrochemical methane oxidation enables modular operation, lower capital costs, and integration with renewable energy sources. Advances in catalyst design, reaction pathways, and reactor configurations have improved selectivity, Faradaic efficiency, and production of C 1 -C 3 oxygenates such as methanol, formic acid, ethanol, and propanol. However, ambient-condition electrochemical methane oxidation remains constrained by coupled catalyst-, reactor-, and separation-level challenges, including limited methane conversion, target-product selectivity, methane delivery, surface oxygen control, suppression of oxygen evolution reaction, and downstream separation. This review examines recent progress in catalyst function, surface oxygen sources, electrolyte chemistry, and reactor architecture, emphasizing the interplay of catalyst behavior and reactor design. The synthesis of experimental and mechanistic insights highlights principles such as three-phase interface engineering, flow reactors, bifunctional catalysts, and scale-up strategies alongside technoeconomic considerations for industrial translation.

title: Nano-architecturing electroactive porous transport layers to reduce voltage losses in anion-exchange membrane electrolyzers
abstract: Anion-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs) offer a promising pathway for sustainable hydrogen production. Despite notable progress, overall system efficiency remains limited, with most research focused on improving membranes and catalysts. However, the design and morphology of porous transport layers (PTLs), a key component in this system, remain less explored and not sufficiently understood. Herein, we address the fabrication of nanoporous spongy architectures on a variety of Ni-based PTLs, including felts, foams, and micropillar structures, by controlled thermochemical redox treatments. A wide range of oxidation and reduction conditions is systematically investigated using ex situ and in situ microscopic analyses to identify optimal configurations of the architecture. The spongy Ni felts show superior electrochemical performance in AEMWEs compared to bare felt, with an ∼2 times higher current density at 2.0 V, a reduced ohmic overpotential of ∼18 mV, a kinetic overpotential of ∼26 mV, and a significant decrease in mass-transport overpotential of ∼93 mV at 0.5 A cm −2 .

title: RoboCulture enables modular robotic plate-based cell automation
abstract: Automating biological experimentation remains challenging due to the need for millimeter-scale precision and long, multi-step workflows and the dynamic nature of living systems. Current liquid handlers only partially automate workflows, requiring human intervention for plate loading, tip replacement, and calibration, while industrial systems are costly and lack flexibility for research settings. Meanwhile, research in autonomous robotics has yet to bridge the gap for long-duration, failure-sensitive biological experiments. Here, we report RoboCulture, a cost-effective and flexible platform that uses a general-purpose robotic manipulator to automate key biological tasks. RoboCulture performs liquid handling, interacts with laboratory equipment, and leverages computer vision for real-time decision-making based on optical density monitoring. We demonstrate a fully autonomous 15-h yeast culture experiment in which RoboCulture uses vision and force feedback together with a modular behavior tree framework to robustly execute, monitor, and manage experiments.

title: Bio-inspired gradient metamaterials with exceptional mechanical performance
abstract: Gradient design is an effective way to enhance the mechanical performance of metamaterials, while current gradient designs generally offer only uni-gradient enhancement performance. To fully leverage the advantages of gradient design, we report a bio-inspired gradient design strategy derived from gradient microstructures of sunflower stems, creating multi-gradient metamaterials. Through a combination of theoretical analyses, experimental tests, and numerical simulations, we demonstrate that bio-inspired tri-gradient designs achieve exceptional enhancements of mechanical performance. This unique phenomenon breaks the upper limitations of performance of conventional uni-gradient metamaterials. The optimum bio-inspired structure exhibits 199.6% and 558.8% enhancements in energy absorption and stiffness performance compared to existing uni-gradient metamaterials. Furthermore, the generalizability of this bio-inspired gradient design strategy is validated, indicating that the exceptional performance brought by this design concept can be extended to other metamaterials with different topological structures. This discovery provides insights for the structural design of multifunctional metamaterials with exceptional mechanical performance.

title: Simple device modification simultaneously enhances indoor passive evaporative cooling power and duration
abstract: Passive evaporative cooling from a damp cloth or vessel can be used for localized cooling of perishables such as food and medicine, drinking water, and even people. Such applications have two key objectives, which are normally in tension with each other: minimizing the water consumption rate and maximizing the cooling (steady-state temperature swing between the cool cloth and the warm surroundings). Here, we present a simple device that delivers higher performance in both metrics simultaneously by adding a perforated aluminum foil sheet suspended over a stagnant air layer to thermally shield the evaporating surface while also facilitating mass transfer. Experimental results demonstrate a simultaneous 10%–25% increase in temperature swing and 2–3× reduction in water consumption rate as compared to conventional evaporative cooling. This improvement is achieved through careful modeling to optimize the coupled heat and mass transfer through the airgap (thermally insulating and vapor permeable) and perforated foil (infrared reflective and vapor permeable).

title: Mechanistic insights and strategies for advancing electrochemical CO2 reduction to single products
abstract: Despite over a decade of research into the electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide, achieving high selectivity for single, value-added products remains an unresolved challenge. While significant progress has been made in reactor-level performance and activity, our mechanistic understanding of why specific products emerge under different catalytic and interfacial conditions is often fragmented or contradictory. Most existing reviews categorize results by broad product classes or specific catalyst levers, often failing to resolve the critical mechanistic branching points between similar multicarbon products. Consequently, the field lacks a coherent, predictive structure that connects elementary reaction steps and microenvironmental effects to single-product selectivity. This manuscript addresses this gap by introducing a descriptor-based, multidimensional framework designed to unify the mechanistic origins of both C 1 and C 2+ pathways. Rather than merely cataloging performance, this approach identifies selectivity-determining intermediates to establish rules that transcend individual material systems. By reconciling long-standing debates and bridging molecular-scale mechanisms with practical system design, we herein provide the necessary foundation for the rational development of next-generation electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction technologies.

title: Synthetic bacterial communities as synergistic anti-corrosion agents
abstract: Marine corrosion causes significant economic and safety issues, driving demand for sustainable alternatives to toxic chemical inhibitors. This study evaluates a rationally designed synthetic consortium for marine corrosion protection. Combining biofilm-forming Bacillus subtilis with Vibrio species representing the natural seawater microbiome yielded protection for carbon steel and black iron that was significantly superior to that of individual strains or sterile controls. Mechanistically, members of the Vibrio consortium induce transcription from the B . subtilis ureA-C promoter. This triggered ureolytic activity facilitates the synergistic deposition of a dense, magnesium- and aragonite-rich mineral layer that passivates the metallic substrate. Electrochemical characterization confirms that this biomineral-biofilm interface effectively inhibits interfacial electron transfer. These findings demonstrate the idea that integrating microbial genetic and electrochemical properties can produce self-regenerating, non-toxic biocoatings, offering a sustainable, long-term solution for protecting marine infrastructure against seawater-induced degradation.

title: Perovskite databases analysis using machine learning and large language models for prediction and reverse engineering
abstract: Perovskite solar cells have reached power conversion efficiencies exceeding 26.95% in single-junction devices and 34.85% in silicon/perovskite tandems, but stability remains a major barrier to commercialization. Here, we report machine learning and large language model (LLM)-based frameworks for analyzing open-access perovskite datasets to address both efficiency and stability challenges. Classical regression models and LLMs are combined to evaluate different data representations, embedding strategies, and hyperparameter configurations for predictive and inverse design tasks. LLMs are further employed to generate fabrication procedures targeting specific key performance indicators, while clustering analysis identifies trends associated with high efficiency and stability. The proposed approach produces optimized recommendations for stack materials, additives, and processing steps across complete perovskite solar cell fabrication, achieving predicted energy yields exceeding 4,000 kWh/m 2 . These results demonstrate the potential of LLM-assisted frameworks for accelerating the discovery and optimization of perovskite solar cells.

title: Overcoming mechanical stability-flow processability trade-off of vitrimers using ionic interactions
abstract: It is well established that the macroscopic flow of dynamic covalent networks involves mesoscopic rearrangement of crosslinkers; however, its relationship with local, segmental motions remains under debate. In this vein, the present study investigates how tuning the segmental (α) dynamics using salt doping impacts the viscoelastic behavior of two vinylogous urethane-based vitrimers. Our analyses show that additional ionic interactions significantly slow down the α relaxation in these materials, driving them into the glassy state at room temperature, while having a much weaker impact on their global dynamics. This disparity allows the separation of the individual contributions of segmental dynamics and network rearrangements to their terminal flow. In addition, our results demonstrate that tuning segmental dynamics, as an alternative to the popular approach of adjusting network rearrangements, can be used for the development of vitrimers that are mechanically rigid and creep resistant at ambient conditions yet flow-processable at moderately high temperatures.

title: Contact lens bioelectronic platform for non-invasive depression treatment with machine-learning-based evaluation
Durable GeP5-carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries through elastomeric layer stabilization
abstract: Despite the abundance and low cost of sodium, the development of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) is hindered by the lack of stable, high-capacity anodes. Here, we report an elastomeric polydopamine (PDA) coating as a multifunctional interfacial buffer layer for GeP 5 /C composites to enhance structural stability and electrochemical performance. The engineered GeP 5 /C-PDA electrode features a hierarchical core-shell architecture in which the PDA layer accommodates volume expansion, preserves interfacial integrity, and stabilizes the solid-electrolyte interphase during repeated cycling. Consequently, the GeP 5 /C-PDA electrode delivers a high initial discharge capacity of 1,023.7 mAh g −1 at 100 mA g −1 . It retains a capacity of 403.4 mAh g −1 after 200 cycles at 500 mA g −1 and exhibits excellent rate capability. This study demonstrates that integrating an elastomeric PDA layer with a conductive carbon network offers a scalable and effective strategy for developing high-performance alloy-type anodes for next-generation SIBs and practical applications.

title: van der Waals supramolecular transistors
abstract: van der Waals (vdW) interactions play a crucial role in various fields, including self-assembly and electronic devices. However, precisely manipulating intermolecular vdW interactions at the single-molecule level to develop supramolecular transistors remains a central challenge. In this study, we report a supramolecular transistor via electrochemical manipulation of a single molecule to a vdW dimer in nickel bis(dithiolene) (NBTE) junctions using the electrochemical scanning tunneling microscopy break-junction technique. Conductance measurements reveal that NBTE remains monomeric under positive potential but forms negatively charged vdW dimers under negative potential. This single-electron redox-driven transition triggers a ∼700-fold increase in conductance and shifts the transport path from in-plane to cross-plane. Theoretical calculations confirm that the dimer is stabilized predominantly by vdW interactions, further enhanced by electric fields, thereby enabling fine regulation of the transistor's conductance. This work demonstrates the first single-electron supramolecular transistor dictated by intermolecular vdW forces, offering a promising strategy for low-power vdW electronics.

title: Clean ice growth from brine by directional freezing
abstract: Directional freezing of brine typically produces porous ice with trapped brine pockets. Previous theories of removing impurity suggest that, for cases such as ice where ions are mostly excluded from the lattice, the freezing rate to grow clean ice from brine approaches zero. Here, we report that clean ice can be produced in a single cycle with a purity exceeding 99.99% (four nines), and a second cycle raises the purity to nearly 7 N (seven nines), indicating its excellent feasibility of separating substances with low partition coefficients. Higher temperature gradients and lower salinity yield faster clean ice growth. A model coupling heat and mass transfer alongside phase equilibrium can accurately predict ice growth and the onset of brine entrapment. These results enhance our understanding of directional freezing in binary systems and open opportunities for multiple fields, such as freezing desalination, metal recovery, protein crystallization, pharmaceutical processing, and other similar settings.

title: Reporting for reproducibility in electrocatalysis
abstract: In this Q&A, expert electrochemists Ezra L. Clark and María Escudero-Escribano discuss the importance of reproducibility in electrocatalysis, best practices for reliable reporting, and what the broader scientific community can do to elevate reporting standards across the field.

title: Integrative structural and computational analysis reveals potential design principles for efficient PROTAC degraders
abstract: Proteolysis targeting chimeras (PROTACs) degrade proteins by recruiting E3 ligases to form ternary complexes, yet the determinants of degradation efficiency remain poorly understood. Here, we report an integrative molecular-dynamics-based framework that combines molecular surface characterization and interaction analyses to investigate PROTAC structure-degradability relationships. Across diverse PROTAC systems, the framework captures how single-molecule stability, complex interactions, and ternary complex dynamics collectively shape degradation outcomes, while lysine topology defines the geometric requirements for productive ubiquitination. Guided by these principles, we design and synthesize optimized CDK12 degraders, and the best degrader achieves a DC 50 of 6.5 nM and a D max of 98.5%, representing an approximately 4-fold improvement in potency. Together, our results establish an interpretable predictive framework for PROTAC design and demonstrate the utility of molecular dynamics simulations in PROTAC optimization.

title: Optoelectronic device geometries for maximizing photocurrent and flexibility
abstract: Flexible silicon micromembranes have gained considerable interest as leadless optoelectronic tissue-stimulation devices. To make these microscale silicon films both flexible and stretchable, they are patterned into serpentine, horseshoe, and spiral shapes, among others. However, all these strategies present a trade-off between flexibility and the device's overall surface area. Although this is not a major concern for traditional flexible electronics, an optoelectronic device's performance depends on its overall surface area. Here, we explore geometric strategies to optimize the photoelectrochemical performance of thin silicon membranes without compromising their flexibility and stretchability. Computational modeling and mechanical testing demonstrated that island elements increasing the device area can be connected "out-of-line" without increasing stiffness. Additionally, spiral-shaped interconnects increased both the area and flexibility of the device by increasing the number of spiral cycles. Characterization of the photogenerated current distribution above the devices confirms a higher photocurrent yield for high-fill-factor geometries. Lastly, employing the membrane designs for optoelectronic modulation of an isolated rat heart demonstrated that higher membrane fill factors reduced the optical power pacing threshold.

title: Fibroblast alignment is governed by stiffness interfaces in hydrogels
abstract: Transitions in mechanical properties between different tissue extracellular matrices are common in the body and influence cellular orientation. For example, in teeth, the abrupt transition between soft dental pulp (∼5 kPa) and stiff dentin (>100 kPa) directs the alignment of odontoblasts. In this study, hydrogels with defined mechanical transitions were used to evaluate the phenotypic response of fibroblasts to soft/soft (3/3 kPa) or soft/stiff (3/200 kPa) interfaces. Near the soft/soft interface, fibroblasts aligned in a parallel-like fashion to the interface (11° angle), compared to the more perpendicular fashion (69° angle to the interface) observed at the soft-stiff interface. Notably, regions of alignment also showed an increased proportion of alpha smooth muscle actin (αSMA)-positive cells, indicating myofibroblast differentiation in response to the mechanical transition. These findings demonstrate that introduction of an interface as a biomaterial mechanical modification, without changes to the biochemical environment, is enough to alter cellular bioactivity.

title: Knowledge-graph attention network ChemFlow identifies modulators of EGFR
abstract: Knowledge-graph drug-target interaction (DTI) models usually assume that test compounds are already represented in the graph, which limits their use for external chemical libraries. Here we present ChemFlow, which addresses this gap by encoding drugs from molecular structure with GATv2 and proteins from fold-specific BioKG RotatE embeddings, preserving protein-side biological context without requiring compound-side graph connectivity. We evaluate ChemFlow with node-masked held-out-compound splits, where test drugs and all incident graph edges are removed before training. Across BioKG, Therapeutic Target Database (TTD) Approved, TTD Approved + Phase, and post-2020 validation, ChemFlow improves precision-recall performance relative to sequence-based, descriptor-based, and docking baselines, including under class-imbalance settings. We then use ChemFlow to screen MedChemExpress compounds against epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Model scoring, docking, and molecular dynamics prioritize allitinib, SYHA-1813, and GNF-2. Cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and EGFR phosphorylation assays support direct target engagement and separate inhibitor-like from agonist-like signaling effects. ChemFlow therefore connects drug-inductive DTI prediction with experimentally testable compound prioritization.

title: Bioabsorbable nanofiber sheets for localized and sustained delivery of therapeutic vesicles
abstract: Targeted drug delivery remains a major challenge in cancer therapy, as systemic administration often causes off-target toxicity and insufficient drug exposure at disease sites. Although lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enhance drug stability and circulation, their systemic use frequently results in limited tumor accumulation. Here, we present bioabsorbable nanofiber (BNF) sheets as a localized, biodegradable platform for sustained LNP delivery. BNF sheets entrap LNPs within their fibrous matrix through capillary-driven closure during drying and release them upon rehydration, enabling spatially confined therapeutic exposure. In a murine ovarian cancer peritoneal dissemination model, BNF sheets loaded with carboplatin-encapsulated LNPs achieved effective local tumor suppression with minimal systemic toxicity, while confirming localized LNP distribution and complete bioabsorption. This approach integrates the molecular versatility of LNPs with site-specific administration, addressing key limitations of systemic nanomedicine. This platform effectively bridges systemic nanomedicine and localized therapy, offering a clinically translatable approach for precision drug delivery.

title: Bioinspired and biomimetic cancer-cell-derived membrane nanovesicles for preclinical tumor-targeted nanotheranostics
abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1016/j.xcrp.2023.101648.].

title: Robust altermagnetic band splitting and non-topological origin of magneto-transport in CrSb thin films
abstract: Altermagnetic materials combine zero net magnetization with large spin splitting, offering new material platforms for spintronics. As the leading altermagnetic candidate, CrSb has been predicted to be a Weyl semimetal but lacks experimental evidence. Here, we report the controllable fabrication of high-quality CrSb (000 l ) thin films, leveraging optimized growth parameters and a novel Cr 2 SbTe buffer layer. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements provide definitive evidence of g -wave altermagnetic order, revealing a large band splitting of 0.54 eV near E F . The surface and altermagnetic band splitting are remarkably robust in CrSb thin films, as demonstrated from aspects of long-term storage, protective passivation layer strategy, and film thickness dependence. Moreover, magneto-transport measurements find no hallmark signatures of Weyl fermions, including the absence of negative chiral magnetoresistance and the specific scaling behavior of the planar Hall effect (PHE). This work establishes high-quality CrSb thin films as a robust platform for exploring altermagnetic phenomena and spintronic devices.

title: Performance and durability trade-offs in low-iridium catalyst layers for PEM water electrolysis
abstract: To deploy proton-exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzers at a gigawatt scale, the iridium-specific power density must be reduced to below 0.1 mg Ir W −1 . Significant variability in reported performance and durability benchmarks makes it difficult to define clear pathways for technological improvement. Here, we report a device-level investigation combining multimodal diagnostics with long-term durability testing across four commercial catalysts at loadings from 0.1 to 0.8 mg Ir cm −2 . While all catalysts achieve the 0.1 mg Ir W −2 target, this cannot be met at lower heating value-based efficiencies above 75% through catalyst design alone. Durability testing over 500 and 1,000 h shows that degradation rates decrease with extended operation and that each catalyst exhibits distinct, loading-dependent behavior. Postmortem characterization confirms progressive catalyst crystallization as a primary contributor to kinetic degradation. These findings demonstrate that future deployment targets depend far more on reducing cell resistance and ensuring long-term durability than on advancing intrinsic catalyst activity.

title: Accounting for dynamic nanomaterial behavior in toxicological study design
abstract: Engineered nanomaterials are known to undergo dynamic physicochemical changes after synthesis. During dispersion, environmental aging, and biological exposure, they can agglomerate, dissolve, undergo surface complexation, acquire biomolecular coatings, or form secondary phases, converting a nominal single-material exposure into a time-dependent mixture of particles, dissolved species, and interfacial states. Although nanomaterial transformation is well established, its consequences are not yet considered consistently in toxicological study design and interpretation. Here, I argue that future studies should focus on four practical decisions: defining the material state at exposure start, recording conditioning and exposure history where it may alter interpretation, targeting early transition measurements when transformations may change the dominant response driver or delivered dose, and selecting a mechanism-relevant dose metric. Minimum reporting is a cross-cutting requirement across all four decisions. This approach is applicable across material classes, including dissolving metal and metal oxide nanomaterials, environmentally aged silver nanoparticles, persistent carbonaceous nanomaterials, and emerging porous materials such as metal-organic frameworks, and shifts attention from the pristine material toward the material state actually presented to the biological or environmental test system.

title: Knee-inspired continuum robots using antagonistic-blocking strategy for torsional and bending stiffness enhancement
abstract: Continuum robots often exhibit positioning errors due to insufficient constraints and underactuation. Inspired by the three-dimensional tension network of biological knee joints, here we report a hierarchical stiffness-decoupling strategy to regulate torsional stability and bending stiffness. A knee-inspired joint with bilateral cross-cable constraints and stepped surfaces improves structural stability: cross-cable constraints increase reaction torque by 73%–90%, whereas hybrid constraints increase it by 171% at 45° and by at least 189% at 90°, while reducing radial perturbation by 64%. To mitigate load-induced displacement in constant-total-tendon-length systems, we further introduce a hybrid enhanced stiffness (HES) strategy combining a blocking mechanism with antagonistic actuation. HES improves apparent stiffness by 51%–131% under tested force-displacement conditions and exceeds the baseline (BN)-corrected arithmetic sum of blocking-enhanced stiffness (BES) and antagonistic-enhanced stiffness (AES) by 4%–35%, indicating nonlinear synergy. This bioinspired approach reduces coupling among compliance, torsional stability, and load-bearing capacity.

title: Polymeric nanogels and hybrid platforms for redox modulation from ROS biology to therapeutic design
abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) play a dual role in biological systems. At physiological levels, they act as essential signaling mediators regulating immune responses, metabolism, proliferation, and differentiation. Conversely, excessive ROS production overwhelms antioxidant defenses, driving oxidative stress, inflammation, and tissue damage. Understanding the generation, spatial confinement, and kinetics of ROS is therefore critical for designing effective therapies. Conventional small-molecule scavengers show limited translational success due to poor stability, rapid clearance, and lack of targeting, while synthetic antioxidants, although more versatile, still face delivery constraints. In this context, polymeric nanogels provide hydrated nanoscale networks capable of protecting labile scavengers, hosting catalytic redox centers, and responding dynamically to ROS-rich microenvironments. However, their standalone application is often limited by insufficient retention in dynamic tissues. To overcome these limitations, hybrid systems integrating nanogels within hydrogels or composite matrices have emerged, enabling improved localization and sustained redox modulation.

title: Palm-sized condensation chamber for the detection and preservation of airborne particles and volatiles
abstract: Characterizing airborne particles and volatiles is critical to many applications, such as non-invasive healthcare, environmental surveillance, and scent analysis. However, due to their inherently low concentrations, gas sensing often requires bulky, expensive instruments, such as gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, to achieve the required sensitivity. Gas-to-liquid conversion via atmospheric condensation has recently emerged as a simple, low-cost sampling strategy capable of capturing both particles and volatile compounds. Here, we present the miniaturized airborne particle/volatiles localization engine (MAPLE), a low-cost, palm-sized device that makes high-sensitivity gas analysis accessible to the general population outside research labs. Through systematic thermofluidic design, MAPLE achieves a low cost ($50), compact form factor (5 cm), and high sampling rate (200 L/min). We demonstrate MAPLE across several real-world applications, including allergen detection, food spoilage monitoring, and non-invasive healthcare through exhaled breath. Beyond detection, MAPLE also enables scent preservation, with potential applications in immersive virtual reality and attribution purposes.

title: Strategy evolution on interdependent networks
abstract: Cooperation is essential to the prosperity of human and biological systems. Its emergence depends on not only on the structure of interactions within a single system but also the coupling between interdependent systems. While the analytical theory for strategy evolution in isolated systems is well established, the effect of coupling has been studied mainly through specific models and simulations. Here, we develop a general analytical framework for strategy evolution on interdependent networks with arbitrary within-system structures and cross-system coupling. We derive the explicit condition under which natural selection favors cooperation and show that coupling can promote cooperation even when no isolated system sustains it. Cooperation is maximized under weak but non-zero coupling, while excessively strong interdependence suppresses it. Cooperation is further enhanced when strategy updating is biased toward the larger or less cooperation-prone system. Our analysis explains when and why coupling promotes cooperation.

title: Crossflow air purification across kirigami-structured menisci
abstract: The capture of particulate matters is at the heart of air pollution control for global health. Laden particles are sieved by fibrous filters, disposables that are unsustainable and cost-prohibitive for wide deployment. Here, we show that tangentially introducing polluted air across arrayed liquid menisci rising on structured kirigami effectively removes these laden particles. Approaching a meniscus, the airflow splits into two lateral branches that form counter-rotating helical vortices. This flow pattern repeats across downstream menisci, generating collective, low-speed vortices that entrain and sweep particles onto the liquid surface for irreversible absorption. This crossflow configuration prevents clogging and flux degradation, yielding a removal efficiency that increases with filter length. A 140-cm-long meniscus filter achieves a sustained filtration velocity of ∼1 m s −1 , an efficiency of 80%, and a negligible pressure drop of ∼10 Pa. This simple approach potentially promises a sustainable air purification solution for resource-poor settings.

title: Applying a spectral encoding-decoding framework for parallel multi-frequency selective excitation for NMR spectroscopy
abstract: Selective one-dimensional (1D) NMR experiments isolate targeted resonances in complex spectra, but conventional implementations acquire one target at a time and therefore become inefficient when multiple sites are of interest. Here, we report SPEED, an application of established spectral encoding and decoding to parallel multi-frequency selective NMR. In this implementation, polychromatic selective pulses are phase encoded, and target-resolved spectra are reconstructed from composite acquisitions. This implementation preserves the correlation information and phase-sensitive line shapes of parent selective experiments, provides the expected N signal-to-noise benefit under matched encoding conditions, and can be inserted into selective 1D CLIP-COSY and 1D NOESY workflows without changing their coherence-transfer logic. Applications to amino acid mixtures, menthol, 17β-estradiol, and ex vivo samples of human serum and pig brain tissue extracts demonstrate simultaneous acquisition of multiple selective correlation spectra, faster measurement, improved sensitivity use, and reliable target-resolved analysis in chemically and biologically complex samples.

title: Explainable AI reveals the allosteric blind spot in protein-ligand binding predictions
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed prediction of protein structure and interactions, yet modeling of allosteric binding remains a persistent challenge. We develop an explainable AI framework that interrogates AI models AlphaFold3, Protenix, Boltz-2, Chai-1, and DynamicBind on rigorously stratified datasets of orthosteric and allosteric ligand-protein complexes. While AI models excel in accurate modeling of orthosteric ligand binding, a consistent and substantial performance gap observed across diverse architectures emerges in prediction of allosteric complexes. The biophysical logic for this dichotomy is unveiled through physics-based lens of the energy landscape theory. Orthosteric binding creates dominant energetic funnels via ligand-induced minimal frustration quenching, while allosteric sites preserve neutral frustration landscapes in both apo and holo protein states. By linking prediction outcomes to frustration landscapes, this study recasts AI shortcomings in prediction of allosteric ligand binding as diagnostic indicators of allostery, establishing a physics-informed framework that turns the allosteric blind spot into mechanistic insight.

title: Flexible polymer-based electromagnetic functional materials in the intelligent era
abstract: With rapid advances in electronics and communications, traditional electromagnetic functional materials (EFMs), constrained by their passive singular function, limited physical forms, and processing methods, can no longer meet the demands of the intelligent era. Consequently, EFMs are undergoing an iterative transformation toward multifunctionality, deviceization, and systematization. Flexible polymer-based materials, owing to their processing adaptability and structural conformability, have emerged as important platforms for achieving functional integration. Grounded in the current state of flexible polymer-based EFMs in the intelligent era, we systematically elucidate their innovative theories, design strategies, and device fabrication methodologies. It comprehensively summarizes the emerging demands that key application scenarios place on EFMs, identifies the bottlenecks encountered during this evolutionary process, and proposes potential solutions. Finally, it provides a forward-looking perspective on future directions for EFMs. Ultimately, we not only offer a systematic framework for the development of EFMs but also delineate an expandable pathway for their advancement.

title: Flexible hybridization of interstitial electrons with a transition metal center
abstract: In inorganic electrides, free electrons usually occupy empty spaces surrounded by irreducible cations such as alkali earths. Here, we report on the unique hybridization of interstitial electrons with Mn/Fe d orbitals in certain known A 6 M N 5 compounds. Calculations show these electrons reside in axial positions 1.83 Å from the metal of [ M N 3 ] ( M = Mn, Fe) units, resulting in a trigonal bipyramidal [ M N 3 (e – ) 2 ] unit. Despite the metal proximity, the oxidation state of Mn and density of states in comparison to related Ca 3 MnN 3 and Ba 3 MnN 3 calculations show this localization to be of distinct electrons, rather than metal nature. Partial density of states and group theory show that, unlike hydride, the interstitial electron ligand can hybridize not only with metal d z 2 but also with d xz and d yz orbitals by using mixed electride 2 s -2 p states. These findings help us understand new properties such as magnetism from anionic electrons within rich transition metal chemistry.

title: Fusing generative AI and ML-FFs for inverse design and high-fidelity dynamic simulation of fused-ring aromatic hydrocarbons
abstract: Rational design of fused-ring aromatic hydrocarbons is hindered by vast chemical space, costly quantum simulations, and a disconnect between generation and dynamic validation. Here, we report an integrated computational platform that unifies physics-constrained generative AI, interpretable multi-objective screening, and high-fidelity machine-learning force fields (ML-FFs) to enable inverse design and dynamic simulation of fused-ring aromatic hydrocarbons. A physical consistency module incorporating the Brown-Ladner method and iterative molecular weight inversion enforces chemical and structural feasibility from the outset, generating diversity, novelty, and theoretically synthesizable structures validated against experimental benchmarks, while XGBoost predictors accurately forecast key electronic properties. We further developed DeepAsphalt-26, ML-FFs specifically optimized for aromatic systems, which attains density-functional-theory-level accuracy while accelerating molecular dynamics by two orders of magnitude, accurately reproducing π-π stacking dynamics and free energy landscapes. By bridging generative design and high-fidelity simulation, this workflow offers an end-to-end in silico route to engineering carbonaceous materials with targeted properties.

title: Passive temperature-adaptive materials for opaque building envelopes toward all-season energy saving
abstract: While passive radiative cooling effectively mitigates summer cooling loads, its static spectral properties often cause a winter heating penalty. Passive temperature-adaptive materials (TAMs) resolve this mismatch through autonomous, zero-energy spectral regulation. Focusing on opaque building envelopes, this review systematically categorizes TAMs based on their structural mechanisms and statistically evaluates the optical performance of each category. Building on these performance insights, we trace the technological evolution from single-band modulation to ideal dual-band synergy, which maximizes summer heat rejection while enhancing winter solar gain and suppressing radiative loss. Crucially, recognizing the distinct operational physics of TAMs compared with static radiative cooling materials, we propose a specialized benchmarking framework to accurately evaluate their dynamic thermal performance. Beyond mechanisms, we critically evaluate engineering barriers for large-scale deployment, specifically weatherability, aesthetic integration, and eco-friendliness. Finally, we highlight the expansion of TAMs to greenhouses, vehicles, and smart textiles.

title: Modular plug-and-play crosslinking platform for precision-engineered hydrogels
abstract: Hydrogels are promising for biomedical applications due to their tunable properties and extracellular matrix (ECM)-mimicking capabilities, but available chemistries limit customization potential. We present a modular bioconjugation system using polyphenol radical crosslinking, where gallic acid (GA)-modified glycosaminoglycans rapidly crosslink with diverse biomolecules under blue light and riboflavin. This method enables the creation of customizable, cell-compatible matrices. We validate conjugation chemistry using 1 H NMR, size-exclusion chromatography, and gel electrophoresis. As proof-of-concept, we have created injectable hydrogels from GA-modified hyaluronic acid (HA-GA) crosslinked with various proteins. Mechanical properties are tunable via riboflavin concentration and light exposure. HCT116 colon cancer cells form spheroids in HA-GA-BSA, while other protein-containing hydrogels support dispersed growth, indicating enhanced cell adhesion. HA-GA hydrogels upregulate stemness markers compared to 2D culture, while protein incorporation reduces this effect. Matrix-activated Wnt signaling confirms functional biomolecule integration using HA-GA-Wnt3A matrices. This strategy enables tailored ECM design for tissue engineering and 3D cell culture.

title: A geometry-aware and customizable multimodal sensing system for texture and material identification in prosthetics
abstract: The restoration of natural somatosensation remains largely absent in upper-limb prostheses. Current electronic skins are still limited by coarse resolution, planar form factors, and high fabrication cost. Here, we present a geometry-aware and customizable multimodal sensing system for prostheses that functions as a sensing component for mimicking human skin. The system integrates high-resolution and high-rate pressure and temperature mapping in conformal, free-form modules. A "scan-model-print" workflow converts a patient's prosthesis topography into 3D sensor curvature for seamless surface conformity. Self-aligning snap-fit interconnects enable on-demand reconfiguration, while interlaced pressure and temperature matrices maximize spatial utilization. Compared with commercial glove sensors, the system achieves ∼10-fold finer spatial resolution for pressure and temperature. A multihead neural network performs real-time calibration and denoising, thereby reducing per-pixel error and improving signal fidelity. The system enables texture and material identification and provides a sensing platform toward personalized prostheses with integrated sensing and haptic feedback.

title: Arylxenonium(II) ions as tunable noble-gas-based Lewis acids
abstract: Noble-gas compounds are traditionally associated with a strong oxidizing character; however, cationic species can also act as Lewis acids. Here, we introduce arylxenonium(II) ions [RXe] + as systematically tunable noble-gas-based Lewis acids, demonstrating that their acceptor strength can be modulated by the fluorination degree and substitution pattern of the aryl group R, in close analogy to classical carbocations or iodonium platforms. By means of a combined theoretical (fluoride and hydride ion affinities, lowest unoccupied molecular orbital [LUMO] energies, and global electrophilicity index) and experimental (Gutmann-Beckett method and 129 Xe NMR spectroscopy) investigation, a quantitative and multidimensional assessment of their Lewis acidity is provided. Fluorine substituents in ortho positions of the aryl group exert a decisive influence on the acceptor ability of these species and play a crucial role in the formation of unprecedented O-donor [RXe···OPEt 3 ] + adducts, otherwise unobservable. Collectively, these results establish a noble-gas-based set of species as a family of cationic Lewis acids with adjustable acceptor properties.

title: Light-induced selectivity of photoelectrochemical glycerol oxidation using BiVO4 photoanodes
abstract: The photoelectrochemical (PEC) glycerol oxidation reaction (GOR) provides a sustainable route to convert biomass waste into value-added chemicals, but controlling product selectivity remains a key challenge. In this study, we show that light intensity influences PEC GOR selectivity on BiVO 4 photoanodes. Increasing illumination from 5 to 100 mW/cm 2 shifts the reaction from partial oxidation products—glyceraldehyde (GLAD), glycolaldehyde (GCAD), and dihydroxyacetone (DHA)—toward the deeply oxidized product formic acid (FA). Frequency-resolved measurements, including intensity-modulated photocurrent spectroscopy and PEC impedance spectroscopy, reveal that higher light intensities enhance surface hole accumulation and interfacial charge transfer, enabling multi-electron oxidation pathways. Control experiments further elucidated the reaction mechanism, identifying GLAD as the primary precursor to FA and GCAD as a secondary intermediate that is further oxidized under higher illumination. These findings provide important insights into the selective control of the PEC GOR, offering a potential strategy for optimizing product distribution in solar-driven biomass valorization and chemical synthesis.

title: Concentration-dependent restructuring of the Eigen-Zundel ensemble revealed by a solvation-state map of the hydrated proton
abstract: Proton transport in aqueous environments underlies processes ranging from biological energy conversion to electrochemical energy storage, but the microscopic mechanisms remain challenging to elucidate. Here, we establish a solvation-state map of aqueous acids that quantitatively links vibrational signatures to concentration-dependent populations of fully solvated ions, solvent-shared ion pairs (SSIPs), and contact ion pairs (CIPs) using vibrational spectroscopy, ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, and quantum mechanical calculations. By identifying the high-frequency O–H stretching band as a sensitive reporter of solvation topology, we show how ion pairing reshapes the free-energy landscape governing proton sharing and localization. Cluster calculations reveal that fully solvated protons adopt a broad conformational ensemble, SSIPs are stabilized in a deep asymmetric potential well, and CIPs collapse into a single-well, Eigen-like state. This framework provides a basis for interpreting proton transport barriers in concentrated electrolytes and aqueous interfaces, offering insight into proton-conducting materials and ion-regulated environments.

title: Strain-release photocatalytic access to rigidified isosteres of bicyclic heterocycles
abstract: We present the synthesis of fused isoxazolidine-pyrrolidine architectures via a dual rigidification strategy. These frameworks are accessed through an atom-economical approach using variously substituted isoxazolines and bicyclo[1.1.0]butane (BCB) derivatives under mild conditions. Subsequent functionalization of these analogs enables the synthesis of structurally diverse, disubstituted bridged pyrrolidines and proline derivatives that are otherwise challenging to access. This approach efficiently generates complex, rigid scaffolds, thereby expanding the chemical space available for the design of medicinally relevant small molecules.

title: Isothermal mass diffusion of sodium chloride and bovine serum albumin in human blood plasma at room temperature
abstract: Despite their importance, mass diffusion data for species in human blood plasma (HBP) remain scarce. Here, we developed a shearing-cell configuration with interferometric setups to measure the effective mass diffusion coefficient of a solute in viscous multicomponent solutions, including HBP. Diffusion coefficients of NaCl and bovine serum albumin (BSA) were measured in benchmark multicomponent systems and HBP. This work shows that under the same Na + concentration, the effective mass diffusion coefficient of NaCl in HBP is 2.8% lower than in water. The small difference supports using binary mass diffusion data as an approximation of salt diffusion in HBP. In contrast, the effective mass diffusion coefficient of BSA, a plasma protein, in HBP is about 67% lower than that in binary aqueous solutions under the same concentration and temperature. The significant difference suggests that protein binary diffusion data should not be used as an approximation in HBP because of a stronger protein-solvent interaction.

title: A bacterial bimetallic nanozyme hybrid strategy for enhancing radiotherapy
abstract: Cancer treatment using bacteria has gained attention due to the ability of bacteria to selectively colonize low-oxygen tumor regions, providing opportunities for targeted therapy and immune activation. Here, we report a probiotic-mediated hybrid system that combines Bifidobacterium infantis with a copper-hafnium bimetallic nanozyme. This system delivers the nanozyme to tumors and stimulates immune responses. The nanozyme converts excess hydrogen peroxide in tumors into reactive oxygen species and oxygen, enhancing the effects of radiotherapy. Hafnium ions increase X-ray energy deposition, causing DNA damage and improving therapeutic outcomes. Moreover, the system induces immunogenic cell death and activates a key immune signaling pathway, generating a strong antitumor immune response. This approach effectively integrates bacterial targeting, high atomic number nanomaterials, and enzymatic catalysis, offering a strategy to improve radiotherapy and overcome the limitations of conventional treatments.

title: Immobilization method dictates the photoelectrochemical glycerol oxidation performance of semiconductor catalyst assemblies
abstract: Photoelectrochemistry provides a direct route to convert sunlight into valuable chemicals. However, high-performance photoelectrode architectures often require complicated synthesis steps and expensive instrumentation. Although physical immobilization (e.g., spray coating) of catalyst particles on semiconductors seems to be a simple and universal approach, it is rarely implemented to prepare photoelectrodes. Here, we highlight challenges associated with such deposition strategies and demonstrate the importance of rational photoelectrode design. Specifically, we introduce metal interlayers (Pd, Au, or Ni) between n-type Si and a spray-coated PdAu catalyst. We show that these interlayers are essential for generating photopotential at the interface, while the PdAu catalyst governs C3 selectivity during glycerol oxidation. We also demonstrate that the interlayer determines key performance metrics (e.g., photopotential, photocurrent density, and stability). With this approach, the best-performing PdAu/Au/Si and PdAu/Ni/Si photoelectrodes can deliver high reaction rates (>100 mA cm −2 ) with sufficient stability even at higher illumination intensities (50 suns).

title: A dynamic in vitro left atrial model for assessing appendage occlusion
abstract: Device-related thrombus (DRT) is a serious complication of left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO). In vitro models can support the safety and functionality assessment of LAAO devices but remain elusive. We develop and validate an in vitro left atrium (LA) model recapitulating atrial fibrillation-specific conditions, i.e., pulmonary vein flow waveform, left atrial appendage (LAA) ostium velocity, and LA ejection fraction. We then apply the system for the echocardiographic assessment of the influence of LAAO device type (non-pacifier vs. pacifier type) and position (ostial vs. deep implantation) on the velocities at the LAA ostium and at the device. The results show that ostial implantation eliminates thrombus-prone low-velocity regions at the LAA ostium, whereas deep implantation leads to low velocities at the LAA ostium and at the device, suggesting an increased risk of blood stagnation, a key factor clinically associated with DRT formation. These findings support the use of the model to optimize device design and implantation strategies.

title: Probing true and apparent chemical bonds by atomic force microscopy
abstract: High-resolution atomic force microscopy (HR-AFM) images often show bond-like features between atoms, but when these features reflect true chemical bonds remains unclear. Here, we report a quantitative benchmark showing that, with a CO-functionalized tip, apparent bond-like features appear when the interatomic separation falls below a critical upper limit of 4.4–5.1 Å. This threshold holds across non-bonded CO clusters, an ionic NaCl(100) surface, and a hydrogen-bonded H 2 O hexamer. True bonds are detected only when their electron density is comparable to or greater than that above adjacent atoms, as shown in tolane. We further propose practical criteria to identify true bonds: flat profiles or local maxima at bond centers signify true bonds, whereas local minima indicate a steric origin, and overlap of the tip's van der Waals surface with that of the bond confirms a bond contribution. These results provide a reliable framework for interpreting HR-AFM images.

title: Sound of bubble coalescence
abstract: Acoustic emissions from bubbly flows are widespread, yet the acoustic role of bubble coalescence remains unresolved. While bubble pinch-off is a well-established acoustic source, coalescence is often presumed comparable or even dominant, largely due to difficulty in distinguishing the two events because of their close temporal proximity. Here, we isolate coalescence using synchronized audio-visual measurements, with experiments and simulations spanning scenarios. We show that bubble coalescence produces weak acoustic emissions, resulting in an effectively silent response with amplitudes and radiated energy reduced by one and up to two orders of magnitude, respectively, relative to pinch-off events. This behavior arises from slow liquid-film drainage during coalescence leading to long excitation timescales, which inhibit effective coupling with the bubble's natural oscillation mode. A damped harmonic oscillator model captures this behavior, offering a pathway to simplified frameworks for bubble acoustics that focus on pinch-off, with implications for efficient acoustic diagnostics in multiphase flows.

title: Thermo- vs. electrocatalysis on Fe- and Ru-based cathodes for ammonia synthesis in proton-conducting ceramic cells
abstract: Electrochemical ammonia synthesis in proton-conducting ceramic cells offers an electricity-assisted alternative to the energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process and may enable decentralized NH 3 production. This study compares the performances of Fe- and Ru-based cathodes with similar catalyst loadings on BCZY721 membranes and an active area of 12.57 cm 2 . Under open-circuit voltage (OCV) conditions, Ru exhibited NH 3 synthesis rates nearly two orders of magnitude higher than those of Fe. Under polarization, rates of 5.52 × 10 −8 mol cm −2 s −1 for Ru and 3.03 × 10 −8 mol cm −2 s −1 for Fe were achieved, while increased Ru loading further raised the rate to 7.70 × 10 −8 mol cm −2 s −1 at 475°C. Despite its lower intrinsic activity, Fe showed a substantially stronger relative response to polarization and approached the performance of Ru. These distinct behaviors provide a basis for electrode concepts combining high intrinsic activity with strong polarization responsiveness. Further mechanistic studies are required to clarify the origin of the observed performance differences.

title: In situ electrochemical multi-site engineering in acid-base-conjugated deep eutectic solvents for high-capacity H2S capture
abstract: Conventional aqueous desulfurization processes face issues including solvent evaporation and equipment corrosion. Nevertheless, non-aqueous technologies capable of effectively overcoming these limitations still exhibit deficiencies in the design of desulfurization active sites and the enhancement of sulfur capacity. Here, we report an acid-base-conjugated deep eutectic solvent (TPDES) that spatially isolates tetramethylguanidine and polyoxometalate via hydrogen-bond networks. By incorporating electrochemical treatment, an acid-base-conjugated multi-site-functionalized deep eutectic solvent (ETPDES) system is successfully established by the cathodic in situ generation of choline hydroxide, which exhibits synergistic interactions among three chemical sites for the removal of hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S). The sulfur capacity reaches 29.33 mg H 2 S/g absorbent, maintaining over 99% desulfurization efficiency during 10 h of continuous multi-cycle testing. This work not only overcomes critical bottlenecks in conventional wet desulfurization processes but also pioneers a new paradigm of "site-programmable" solvent design through electrochemical-green chemistry coupling, providing a scalable solution for industrial gas purification.

title: A synergistic fabrication strategy for polymer multilayer gradient high-entropy composites for aerospace applications
abstract: To address the degradation of spacecraft-exposed polymers under the synergistic effects of atomic oxygen (AO) erosion and space debris (SD) impact, we develop a series of (TiAlCrSiV)O x /TiAlCrSiV/(AuNiTi) + -PI(CPI) gradient multilayer composite films using a coupled energetic fabrication strategy. Ion co-implantation (C-IIP) creates chelated mechanical interlocking networks at the polymer interface, significantly enhancing adhesion (1.67 ± 0.21 N·mm −1 ) and fracture toughness. Simultaneously, twin-pulse filter cathode vacuum arc co-deposition (TP-FCVA) and gradient multilayer architecture promote independent component modulation and near-room-temperature optimization of residual stress (−36.07 MPa). This precisely customized composition, combined with mechanical robustness-confers exceptional AO resistance (E y = 4.46 ± 0.19 × 10 −26 cm 3 atom −1 ) and synergistic durability. In addition, the composite films impart significant irradiation resistance and reliable electrostatic dissipation performance. The integration of energetic fabrication and high-entropy interface engineering thereby provides a robust and adaptable pathway for developing next-generation spacecraft materials capable of enduring synergistic space effects.

title: Hydrogen leakage across the value chain
abstract: Hydrogen is widely considered a key energy carrier for net-zero targets, particularly in hard-to-abate sectors, yet its small size and high diffusivity make it prone to leakage across the value chain, raising safety, energy-loss, and climate concerns. This review treats hydrogen leakage as an infrastructure-management problem linking leak pathways, detection capability, climate-relevant accounting, and mitigation. Rather than treating reported values as directly comparable leakage rates, we classify the evidence by system boundary and measurement basis, distinguishing physical leakage from broader operational losses. We synthesize advances in acoustic, optical, and catalytic detection, some reaching parts-per-billion sensitivity; atmospheric-chemistry ensembles assess hydrogen's indirect global warming potential and its dependence on leakage rate, production pathway, and time horizon. We assess mitigation through barrier coatings, sealing materials, and modular design and identify key gaps in leakage quantification, soil-sink uncertainty, long-term material performance, and leakage-specific regulation.

title: A stirred tank flow-electrode reactor for direct lithium extraction from brines
