abstract: Piezoelectric materials, which linearly interconvert mechanical and electrical energy, are ubiquitous in the modern world due to their many forms as sensors, actuators, and energy harvesters. Machine learning methods are emerging as a tool in the search for sustainable high-performance materials, offering the ability to rapidly analyze huge compositional spaces that are beyond traditional trial-and-error exploration. Recently, there has been a marked increase in the rate of publishing rationally designed piezoelectrics, especially methods that integrate machine learning. This review analyzes these recent developments and provides a meta-analysis in the field of machine learning predictions of piezoelectric properties. Collective issues such as limited data reporting and a lack of standardized evaluation metrics are highlighted as roadblocks to meaningful progress in high-accuracy predictions. Finally, some recommendations are made on best-practice methods to remedy these issues going forward—such as more open data sharing as well as standardized use of rigorous model validation schemes.

title: External excitation signal-free online internal parameter identification for proton exchange membrane fuel cell diagnosis
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) technology for proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) is constrained by issues such as test signal interference, hardware redundancy, and lengthy testing. Here, we report an online parameter identification method for characterizing EIS, which eliminates external excitation and hardware redundancy while accelerating EIS extraction. First, the distribution of relaxation time (DRT) is employed to analyze the physical processes, and a mapping is established among DRT-fitted peaks, EIS, the equivalent circuit model (ECM), and electrochemical mechanisms. Furthermore, an identifiable model transformation and parameter decoupling process is designed, and the recursive least squares-H infinity filter (RLS-HIF) algorithm is proposed for online parameter identification. Finally, online parameter identification experiments are conducted to analyze the performance of the RLS-HIF, including dynamic tracking performance, steady-state robustness, and initial value sensitivity. The study demonstrates that the proposed method exhibits excellent performance and provides technical support for online health monitoring of fuel cells.

title: Physics-informed coarse-mesh framework predicts oxidation-corrosion-deposition in lead-bismuth eutectic systems
abstract: Safety assessment of lead-bismuth eutectic (LBE) energy systems requires predicting coupled oxidation, corrosion, and corrosion product deposition across engineering length and time scales. Existing methods rarely combine sufficient accuracy with practical computational cost, and they often neglect feedback from deposited corrosion products. Here, we report a physics-informed coarse-mesh multiphysics framework for oxidation, corrosion, and deposition analysis in LBE systems. The framework couples corrosion product transport and deposition with oxidation, corrosion, and heat transfer. Comparisons with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations and experiments show that it captures key thermohydraulic, mass transfer, oxidation, corrosion, and deposition behavior while reducing central processing unit (CPU) cost by about three orders of magnitude. Full-core simulations of 108 assemblies show that iron-based deposits reduce corrosion removal but increase thermal resistance, while spacer grids either suppress or enhance deposition depending on the dominant mechanism. This framework enables the practical assessment of material degradation and thermal margins in LBE systems.

title: From prediction to understanding: Can artificial intelligence truly learn?
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning (ML) methods are transforming research across the physical sciences. Algorithms capable of truly learning physico-chemical principles could accelerate hypothesis generation and data interpretation and potentially even yield truly novel scientific insights. In this Voices piece, a panel of five experts shares their views on whether current AI/ML methods can truly learn such principles and whether it matters.

title: Why machine learning struggles with magnetism? The role of temperature, disorder, and spin physics
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has transformed materials informatics by enabling rapid prediction, screening, and discovery across vast chemical spaces. However, its application to magnetic materials remains fundamentally constrained. Magnetism presents a particularly stringent representation problem because spin degrees of freedom are coupled to temperature, exchange interactions, spin-orbit coupling, electron correlation, disorder, and microstructure across multiple scales. In contrast, most current ML frameworks rely on static structural or compositional representations, often derived from zero-temperature electronic-structure calculations and ordered materials databases. This mismatch limits their ability to capture the physical mechanisms governing magnetic behavior and frequently reduces prediction to interpolation within restricted datasets. Here, we examine these limitations across major magnetic material classes, including soft magnets, permanent magnets, magnetocaloric materials, two-dimensional magnets, altermagnets, and chemically disordered magnetic systems. We further discuss emerging directions toward physics-informed ML frameworks capable of incorporating thermodynamic evolution, spin interactions, disorder, symmetry, and multiscale magnetic phenomena explicitly.

title: On-demand thermal power amplification enabled by active heat Q-switching
abstract: Thermal energy storage buffers intermittent heat sources, but delivering short bursts on demand requires control over both retention and release. Here, we show that counter-flow heat oscillators provide this control through an actively switchable thermal quality factor, Q . Matched flows sustain internal heat recirculation and energy accumulation; flow detuning or reduced interchannel coupling releases stored energy rapidly. Experiments in a water-based device demonstrate approximately 5-fold enhancement of one channel's outlet power relative to its pre-switch steady output, in agreement with a transient thermofluidic model. The model predicts approximately 20-fold peak amplification relative to input power for liquid-metal systems, with stacked oscillators further extending the accessible energy-power range. These results establish Q -switching as a means of controlling when accumulated thermal energy is delivered, linking resonant heat transport to programmable thermal output.

title: Optoelectronic materials and devices: Advances, challenges, and future directions
abstract: Held in Macau in April 2026, the Cell Press Forum on Optoelectronic Materials and Devices marked the launch of the Sino-Portuguese Joint Laboratory of Optoelectronics and our sister journal Matter & Light . In this Voices piece, Forum speakers share perspectives on emerging technologies, unresolved challenges, and future directions for optoelectronic materials and devices.

title: User-in-the-loop adaptive mechanostimulation using structurally engineered hybrid piezoresistive force sensing
abstract: Repetitive stooping in labor-intensive work induces back muscle fatigue, requiring precise adaptive mechanostimulation. Existing systems suffer from inaccurate force and preload detection, resulting in unstable contact and inconsistent pressure delivery. Here, we present a sensing-driven adaptive mechanostimulation system based on a hybrid piezoresistive force sensor. The sensor integrates a pyramid-microstructured element for high-sensitivity preload detection and a bulk composite element enabling wide force range sensing. The system incorporates a lightweight cable-driven positioning module, a soft therapy actuator, and a wearable robotic framework. This architecture enables precise stimulation of fatigue-related muscles identified via multichannel surface electromyography, while the hybrid sensor provides preload calibration and real-time force regulation, improving contact stability and therapeutic precision. In a controlled study with 15 participants, the system demonstrates significantly better recovery outcomes than thermal stimulation ( p = 0.0025) and preprogrammed mechanostimulation ( p = 0.0003). This work establishes a sensing-driven adaptive mechanostimulation paradigm for interactive fatigue rehabilitation.

title: Ultrasound-activated drug release with extracellular vesicles
abstract: Abstract Precise, noninvasive targeting and controlled drug release to the nervous system could transform both basic research and clinical therapy. In this work, we developed a focused ultrasound–responsive delivery system based on extracellular vesicles (EVs), which are naturally occurring and biocompatible phospholipid nanocarriers. To enable the ultrasound responsiveness, a lipid–gas phase transition material Perfluoropentane (PFP) was co-encapsulated with therapeutic agents into EVs via low-temperature sonication. The resulting EVs had a size of 100–200 nm and demonstrated efficient, on-demand release upon ultrasound stimulation. In primary cultured neurons, EVs loaded with lidocaine successfully suppressed calcium activity and showed minimum cytotoxicity. Finally, we demonstrated in vivo application of this system for modulation pain sensitivity in rats. Our EVs-drugs platform demonstrated a safe, and ultrasound-activated drug delivery with high spatiotemporal control, showing strong potential therapeutic applications.

title: Domain-knowledge-guided active design and transfer learning of high-performance bimetallic composites
abstract: Integrating dissimilar metals into a single load-bearing architecture offers a route to lightweight structural materials with high damage tolerance. Yet, the reliability of reactive bimetallic is constrained by brittle intermetallic compounds (IMCs), triggering premature interfacial fracture. Herein, we develop a domain-knowledge-guided active design framework that integrates mixing-enthalpy and phase-structure descriptors with source-domain generation and target-domain transfer learning to accelerate filler-alloy discovery. This framework identified Cr 1.1 Cu 24.4 Ni 20.3 Ti 3.5 Co 21.8 Fe 20.3 Al 8.6 at.% and Cu 17.6 Ni 17.7 Co 18.0 Cr 18.3 Mo 10.5 Fe 17.9 at.% filler alloys, enabling Ti-Ni and Ti-Fe composites with fracture strengths of 475.44 and 340.07 MPa and stable friction properties. Ti-Ni composites formed a Ti 2 (Ni, Co, Fe)/Ti(Ni, Co, Fe) dual-phase with deformation discrepancies. Ti-Fe composites developed a Ti 2 (Ni, Co, Fe)/Ti(Ni, Co, Fe)/(Mo, Cr) ss multiphase, revealing incoherent interfaces with localized strain. Despite distinct failure pathways, both composites performed outstandingly, attributed to the incorporation of chemically complex IMCs within the proposed framework. This work established a transferable, physics-guided filler design paradigm for bimetallic composites.

title: Hydroalkylation and hydroacylation of trifluoromethyl olefins by N-centered direct hydrogen atom transfer photocatalysis
abstract: The selective functionalization of trifluoromethyl olefins, while keeping the essential trifluoroalkyl moiety intact, remains a synthetic challenge. In this study, we report the use of an acridinium amidate as a direct hydrogen atom transfer (d-HAT) photocatalyst for the mild and selective hydroalkylation and hydroacylation of fluorinated olefins. The unique nature of this type of N -centered radical d-HAT system allows an efficient HAT process with a variety of substrates, as well as a single-electron transfer (SET) to obtain the corresponding α-CF 3 carbanion intermediate, while the undesired, typically occurring β-fluoro elimination leading to gem -difluoroalkanes when employing α-trifluoromethyl alkenes as radical acceptors is suppressed by a facilitated last protonation step. This method gives ready access to trifluoromethyl alkanes and can be extended to other fluorinated olefins and to post- and late-stage modifications of pharmaceutically relevant compounds, expanding the toolbox for sustainable and efficient synthesis of highly functionalized fluorinated derivatives under visible light photocatalysis.

title: Cell-generated forces recapitulate geometry-defined deformation modes in auxetic and non-auxetic micro-architected scaffolds
abstract: Architected scaffolds encode deformation behavior through geometry, enabling auxetic contraction or conventional expansion under applied loading. While these deformation modes are routinely characterized by passive mechanical testing, it remains unclear whether they persist under endogenous, spatially distributed cellular forces. Here, we report the use of "auxetic" and "non-auxetic" elastic, as well as mechanically "stiff" micro-architected scaffolds fabricated by multiphoton lithography to decouple Poisson's ratio from elastic modulus while preserving geometry and porosity. Using neural stem cells as a model system, we show that cell-generated loading produces deformation patterns over time that correspond to those observed under uniaxial compression. Despite fundamentally different loading conditions, transverse deformation remains governed by unit-cell topology, indicating that the geometry-encoded deformation behavior is recapitulated under active cellular loading. This proof-of-concept study supports the predictive value of conventional mechanical characterization for architected biomaterials and provides a framework for investigating architecture-dependent cell-material interactions relevant to tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

title: Precision ultrasound-localized sonoporation equipment enabling intratumoral delivery for cancer immunotherapy
abstract: Abstract Cancer immunotherapy offers a promising long-term treatment for solid tumors by activating the immune system, but side effects and systemic toxicity limit its broad clinical translation. While intratumoral delivery addresses these limitations, elevated stiffness within solid tumors continues to hinder both intracellular and extracellular delivery. Here, a novel therapeutic platform, the Precision Ultrasound-Localized Sonoporation-Equipment (PULSE), is presented to enable spatiotemporally controlled, ultrasound-mediated gene and drug delivery for intratumoral immunotherapy. The PULSE incorporates forward and sideward-looking miniaturized ultrasound transducers, integrated into either a 7-French catheter (cPULSE) or a 16-gauge needle (nPULSE), to minimally invasively sonicate a centimeter-sized tumor. Following the design, prototyping, and characterization of PULSE, its dual capability for intracellular and extracellular delivery is demonstrated through comprehensive in vitro cell-based sonoporation tests and phantom-based drug penetration tests. Luciferase assays (activity: ~10 4 RLU/μg level) in the cell studies confirm significantly enhanced gene transfection with cPULSE, while increased dye diffusion (width: ~1 cm level) in the phantom tests validates improved perfusion with nPULSE. The reported PULSE shows promise for spatiotemporally precise, controlled, and localized therapeutic delivery in early-stage tumors for intratumoral immunotherapy.

title: A glitazone-based chemical platform for mechanistic modulation of amyloid-β aggregation and associated pathology
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) arises from intertwined pathological features, including amyloid-β (Aβ) aggregation, metal ion dyshomeostasis, oxidative stress, and cholinergic dysfunction, yet chemical strategies capable of interrogating and regulating these processes remain limited. Here, we identify glitazone derivatives as chemically tunable small molecules that modulate multiple AD-relevant pathways. Through intermolecular interactions, these compounds alter the aggregation behavior of both metal-free and metal-bound Aβ across distinct assembly stages, attenuating associated cytotoxicity. Integrated biophysical and chemical analyses reveal residue- and conformation-specific interactions between glitazone derivatives and Aβ, accompanied by metal-dependent oxidative modifications. In addition to aggregation control, selected glitazone derivatives exhibit antioxidant activity and acetylcholinesterase inhibition, enabling engagement of multiple pathological targets of AD. Collectively, this work establishes glitazones as a chemically tunable platform for mechanistic investigation and multi-target-directed modulation of amyloid pathology, providing a framework for probing interconnected biochemical processes underlying AD.

title: Phase-regulated sodium-storage properties in CuSe and Cu2Se nanoplate anodes
abstract: Copper selenides are promising anode materials for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), owing to high electronic conductivity, rich phase diversity, and large theoretical capacity. However, their phase-dependent sodium-storage performances remain insufficiently defined. Herein, we report a phase-controlled synthesis of CuSe and Cu 2 Se nanoplates (NPLs) to directly compare their phase-dependent electrochemical behavior. When evaluated as SIB anodes, CuSe NPLs demonstrate superior rate capability and cycling stability relative to Cu 2 Se NPLs, delivering a specific capacity of 368.8 mAh g −1 at 20 A g −1 and maintaining 337.4 mAh g −1 at 10 A g −1 after 1,000 cycles with a capacity decay of only 0.012% per cycle. Operando X-ray diffraction and electrochemical kinetic analyses reveal that sodium storage in CuSe is mediated by coupled diffusion-controlled and pseudocapacitive processes. Collectively, these findings confirm that crystal phase decisively governs sodium-storage chemistry and kinetics in copper selenides and offer guidance for high-performance conversion-type anodes for next-generation SIBs.

title: Rhomboid tiling-based topological deep learning for protein complex structure quality assessment beyond pairwise contacts
abstract: Protein complex structure quality assessment remains challenging, particularly with the rapid advancement of generative models such as AlphaFold3, which can produce plausible yet inaccurate structures. Here, we report rhomboid tiling-based topological deep learning (RT-TDL) for protein complex structure quality assessment. RT-TDL represents protein complexes using a hierarchy of order- k Delaunay graphs that capture order- k interactions and organizes them within the rhomboid tiling framework, enabling information propagation within and across different orders. By explicitly modeling higher-order interactions, RT-TDL also highlights biologically meaningful residue combinations. RT-TDL achieves state-of-the-art performance on major protein complex quality assessment benchmarks and ranks as the top-performing single-model method on the CASP EMA dataset, improving correlation by up to 11.9% over existing approaches. RT-TDL further achieves slightly higher AUC scores than AlphaFold3's self-assessment module, highlighting the potential of higher-order structural representations for protein complex modeling.

title: Accurate non-invasive prediction of battery internal temperature to enhance battery safety
abstract: Thermal runaway in batteries, driven by uncontrolled temperature rise, remains a critical safety challenge, highlighting limitations in temperature monitoring and management. Here, we report a non-invasive internal temperature evaluation method based on in-operando isothermal calorimetry. The method quantitatively characterizes heat generation and evaluates internal temperature gradients under various operating conditions, demonstrating the existence of thermal hysteresis and its dependence on temperature and charge/discharge rates. Applying heat transfer theory to boundary heat flux data obtained from calorimetry enables the evaluation of the internal temperature distribution, whose validity is confirmed through in situ temperature measurements. A geometric approximation further extends the methodology to thermal management applications lacking direct calorimetry capabilities, enabling estimation of internal temperature during discharge. This non-invasive strategy provides reliable reference internal temperatures for safely profiling internal thermal states and guiding the design of advanced battery thermal management systems.

title: DEL-Ranking framework for ranking-aware denoising of DNA-encoded library screens for improved affinity prediction
abstract: DNA-encoded library (DEL) screening links small molecules to unique DNA barcodes, enabling massively parallel measurements of compound-protein interactions in which sequencing read counts serve as surrogates for binding affinity. Converting these counts into reliable affinity estimates remains challenging because stochastic Poisson noise dominates low-abundance compounds, while synthesis, selection, and amplification biases can decouple observed enrichment from true thermodynamic binding strength. Here, we present DEL-Ranking, an integrated computational framework that learns stable relative orderings through complementary pairwise and listwise ranking objectives and incorporates a chemical-referenced correction (CRC) module to recalibrate count predictions using structure-activity priors. Across five carbonic anhydrase datasets, DEL-Ranking consistently improves agreement with experimental K i values, including a 0.304-unit gain in Spearman correlation under high-noise overexpression conditions, and independently prioritizes pyrimidine sulfonamide—a known bioisostere of benzene sulfonamide—without explicit supervision for that scaffold. These results show that coupling ranking-aware denoising with chemically informed correction yields more reliable, interpretable, and validation-ready DEL hit lists.

title: Lightweight MSA design advances protein folding from evolutionary embeddings
Toward automated discovery with generative models multimodal learning and closed loop workflows in inverse materials design
abstract: Inverse materials design is shifting materials discovery from forward prediction to targeted proposal of candidates that satisfy objectives under physical constraints. Here, we review advances in generative crystal structure modeling, multimodal learning, and closed-loop design pipelines for crystalline solids. We compare generative model classes, including variational autoencoders, normalizing flows, and autoregressive and diffusion models, focusing on their inverse design trade-offs, how physical and chemical constraints are imposed, and how reliably generated candidates survive downstream validation. We examine multimodal learning as a design interface connecting structures with properties, characterization, processing context, and scientific text and coupling these representations with latent optimization, Bayesian optimization, reinforcement learning, and active learning to guide search under limited validation budgets. We set out recurring failure modes, including surrogate exploitation, diversity collapse, distribution shift, and the stability-synthesizability gap and define a nine-rung discovery-credibility ladder, proposing a minimum reporting standard specifying evidence required to support credible materials discovery claims.

title: COWFISH2A+ as a versatile and accessible platform for digital bioanalysis
abstract: Digital bioanalysis enables single-molecule detection of biomolecules and holds transformative potential across the life sciences and clinical diagnostics. However, its broader translation remains limited by accessibility and versatility. Here, we present COWFISH2A+, a compact, fully automated device integrating wide-field imaging with a custom dispensing module. Using an open-type microchip, COWFISH2A+ enables diverse assays at low cost through direct liquid deposition. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate two types of digital bioanalysis: a digital enzyme assay and an amplification-free digital genetic assay, SATORI. The digital enzyme assay discriminates alkaline phosphatase, a blood biomarker, at the single-isozyme level with sub-femtomolar sensitivity, while SATORI achieves attomolar-level detection of multiple pathogen-derived genetic targets. Furthermore, to demonstrate the translational potential of SATORI, we directly test 159 clinical specimens, detecting SARS-CoV-2 from nasopharyngeal swabs within ∼20 min with 92% sensitivity and 85% specificity. COWFISH2A+ thus provides an accessible and versatile platform for digital bioanalysis.

title: Evaluating land productivity with semi-transparent colored CdTe thin-film PV and broccoli cultivation in agrivoltaic systems
abstract: Agrivoltaics, which combines solar photovoltaics with agricultural production, offers a promising strategy to address growing demands for food and renewable energy while reducing land-use conflicts. Here, we report the performance of semi-transparent, magenta-colored cadmium telluride photovoltaic panels designed to transmit wavelengths favorable for broccoli growth under outdoor field conditions. We evaluate two panel transparency levels corresponding to average photosynthetically active radiation transmittance values of 13.2% and 19.2% under the investigated designs. Although reduced light delays crop maturity by 25 days, broccoli grown beneath the systems achieves fresh biomass comparable to open-field plants, while increasing radiation use efficiency by up to 4.5-fold. Concentrations of most macronutrients remain unchanged whereas those of micronutrients decrease, indicating altered nutrient dynamics under modified light and microclimatic conditions. These findings showcase that the studied systems have the potential to sustain broccoli yield, while simultaneously generating renewable electricity, although further validation under a broader range of conditions is needed.

title: Passive aerodynamic robustness reduces disturbance amplification in flight
abstract: Although limiting flight responses to flow disturbances is typically considered an active-control problem, birds often sustain fixed-wing gliding in disturbed air, raising the question of whether the wing itself can passively limit these responses. Here, we show that avian wings exhibit passive aerodynamic robustness to disturbances. Compared with a planform-matched rigid airfoil wing, the avian wing exhibits lower lift-response gain, smoother stall transition, reduced force fluctuations, and a broader operating angle-of-attack range across turbulence intensities. These wing-level properties translate into an expanded passive stability envelope in rigid-flyer dynamics. Flow diagnostics associate this robustness with delayed separation and altered distributions of turbulent kinetic energy. This robustness comes at the cost of reduced aerodynamic efficiency, revealing an efficiency-robustness trade-off in disturbed flows. We identify aerodynamic sensitivity and control demand as key metrics for bird-scale flight in turbulence and suggest passive aerodynamic robustness as a design principle for resilient flying systems.

title: A separation-dependent metric for triboelectric adhesion optimization
abstract: Electrostatic adhesion is commonly assumed to reach its maximum at contact under fixed-charge conditions. Here, we reveal that triboelectric adhesion exhibits a separation-dependent response arising from dynamic charge redistribution, with the peak adhesion force occurring at a finite gap rather than at contact. Repeated contact electrification establishes interfacial charges, while resistance-mediated charge transfer between electrodes introduces a delayed electrical response during periodic contact-separation motion. We develop a theoretical framework that couples mechanical motion, charge transfer, and electrostatic interaction, identifying two independent dimensionless parameters governing adhesion optimization. The model distinguishes peak-force-oriented optimization from robustness-oriented optimization based on the minimum adhesion force within a cycle. Vacuum experiments using a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE)-copper interface validate the predicted dynamic adhesion behavior. These findings establish a design principle for enhancing triboelectric adhesion and enabling low-power, repeatable electrostatic interfaces.

title: Opportunities for academic PV module materials innovation beyond the solar cell
abstract: The photovoltaics (PV) industry is producing and deploying solar panels at a record pace, fueled by an unprecedented decrease in manufacturing costs over the past decade. The long-established silicon solar cell has been the foundation of this manufacturing boom. Meanwhile, academic research in PV over the past few decades has largely focused on novel "next-generation" solar cells, which could offer lighter weight and/or lower costs. The combined efforts of researchers have yielded many exciting breakthroughs, including recent interest in perovskite/silicon tandem cells. Still, the focus on cell performance overlooks the multiple remaining materials which comprise a working solar panel. In this perspective, we argue for more academic research focus on silicon PV module materials, which can benefit the industry via performance improvements, cost reductions, and supply chain diversification. Indeed, several key components of today's solar panel technologies are at risk of shortages in the coming decade, threatening to raise manufacturing costs if alternatives are not discovered. Lastly, we highlight several opportunities for material improvements for perovskite/silicon tandem solar panels, which may be necessary to achieve large-area modules with 25-year lifetimes.

title: Suppressing SARS-CoV-2 replication by disrupting frameshifting viral RNA pseudoknot topology through simultaneous stem binding and invasion
abstract: RNA pseudoknots are compact tertiary structures in which coaxially stacked double-stranded (ds) stems are bridged by single-stranded (ss) loops, offering a unique opportunity for programmable molecular recognition. Here, we introduce dual-affinity peptide nucleic acids (daPNAs), which integrate antisense PNA and dsRNA-binding PNA scaffolds within a single oligomer, to target the frameshift-stimulatory pseudoknot in SARS-CoV-2. Binding and mutational data suggest that daPNAs achieve structure-specific, nanomolar recognition via concurrent Watson-Crick strand invasion of Stem2 and Hoogsteen triplex formation with Stem1. daS2PK-1 potently suppresses ribosomal frameshifting in cell-free and cellular systems and reduces SARS-CoV-2 viral RNA replication with minimal cytotoxicity. In contrast, daS2PK-5 binds tightly through triplex formation with Stem2 and partial strand invasion of Stem1, yet shows markedly weaker frameshifting inhibition, likely due to pseudoknot topology preservation and slow co-translational Stem2 folding. daPNAs thus enable site-specific pseudoknot targeting, offering a generalizable platform for the development of structure-specific probes and therapeutics.

title: The active catch-up mechanism of fan worms
abstract: Filter-feeding marine invertebrates have evolved many different mechanisms to capture suspended microscopic food particles, which might inspire imitation (Riisgård and Larsen1), but there is a difference between a bioinspired design, which is more broadly defined and based on “inspiration,” and a biomimetic design, which tries to recreate what the organism is doing.

title: Transformer-based generation of equivalent circuits for electrochemical impedance spectroscopy: EIS-GPT
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is widely used to probe electrochemical systems, with impedance spectra commonly interpreted through regression to equivalent circuit models (ECMs). However, ECM identification remains challenging due to structural non-uniqueness and the reliance on expert-driven model selection. Here, we present EIS-GPT, a transformer-based generative framework for ECM prediction that represents circuits as directed acyclic graphs and constructs candidate topologies autoregressively from impedance data. Reinforcement-learning-based fine-tuning is adapted to guide topology generation through reward functions that favor accurate spectral description while accounting for physical plausibility and model complexity. The framework produces candidate circuits that provide competitive spectral explanations while avoiding overfitting. By formulating ECM discovery as structure-aware generative optimization rather than categorical selection, EIS-GPT provides a scalable and transparent strategy for automated impedance model discovery across diverse electrochemical systems.

title: Toward socio-techno-economic power systems with demand-side flexibility
abstract: Demand-side flexibility in buildings and mobility can facilitate renewable energy integration and reduce power system carbon emissions. Realizing this potential requires advances in energy management, business models, control technologies, markets, and grids, as well as insights from engineering, social science, and economics. This review presents a socio-techno-economic framework connecting end-users, buildings, mobility, control systems, electricity markets, and power grids. We examine the interactions among these elements and highlight the importance of bidirectional information flows and coordinated decision-making. We show that demand-side flexibility cannot be fully realized through siloed approaches but instead requires deeper integration across stakeholders and systems. Finally, we identify research and implementation challenges and outline future directions for renewable-based power systems and control engineering. Maximizing the benefits of demand-side flexibility requires holistic methods for identifying, measuring, and deploying flexibility, supported by transdisciplinary collaboration and commercially viable solutions.

title: Enhancing interpretability of cryo-EM maps using hybrid attention Transformers
abstract: ABSTRACT Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has become a central technique for determining the structures of macromolecular complexes. However, experimental cryo-EM density maps often exhibit limited interpretability due to noise and heterogeneous, anisotropic resolution, complicating downstream atomic model construction. Here we present DEMO-EMReF, a Swin Transformer-based framework specifically designed for cryo-EM density map refinement that integrates channel attention with hybrid spatial attention. By combining local window-based attention with grid-based sparse global attention, DEMO-EMReF captures fine-grained local density features while modeling long-range, cross-region spatial dependencies, enabling more robust density refinement in heterogeneous and anisotropic map regions. DEMO-EMReF was systematically evaluated on large benchmark sets of both primary maps and half-maps spanning resolutions of 3.0-8.0 Å and was compared against multiple state-of-the-art map enhancement methods. DEMO-EMReF consistently improves resolution-related metrics, map-model correlations, and local atomic resolvability, with particularly robust gains in challenging heterogeneous or anisotropic cases. Importantly, the refined maps facilitate more accurate and efficient automated atomic model building. Together, DEMO-EMReF provides a robust approach for enhancing cryo-EM density maps and enabling more reliable downstream studies.

title: Engineering 3D architectures of photothermal nanomaterials for high-performance solar interfacial evaporation
abstract: The global freshwater scarcity crisis is becoming increasingly severe, making the development of efficient and sustainable freshwater production technologies an urgent priority. As a promising solution, solar-driven interfacial evaporation (SDIE) technology has attracted considerable attention from the academic community in recent years. With the absorption rate of sunlight by photothermal nanomaterials approaching its theoretical limit, the importance of rational evaporator structural design is becoming increasingly prominent. Here, we report the research progress of 3D-structure evaporators based on photothermal nanomaterials, systematically exploring the mechanisms and advantages of 3D-structure evaporators in light capture, thermal management, water transport, and salt regulation. Furthermore, we discuss the latest advancements of 3D evaporators in multifunctional applications such as zero liquid discharge (ZLD), complex wastewater treatment, and combined water and power generation. Finally, we explore the current challenges and research gaps in this field and provide an outlook on future development.

title: Moving beyond thermal conductivity to interfacial networks for next-generation coolants
abstract: Cooling technologies are entering a critical era driven by electrification, artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, and renewable energy systems. Conventional coolant design remains rooted in a property-centric framework that independently optimizes thermal conductivity, heat capacity, and viscosity. Emerging evidence, including our own studies of nanoparticle-enhanced fluids, reveals non-Einstein behavior in which heat-transfer performance improves while viscosity decreases, challenging the classical suspension theory. We argue that the next frontier lies in understanding, visualizing, and engineering interfacial networks through which the coolant performance should instead be understood. Such networks include the structures and connections formed from the interactions of molecules, particles, and fluidic layers, which collectively govern coupled heat and momentum transport. Progress will require new operando characterization techniques, quantitative network descriptors, and multiscale modeling, ultimately enabling rational design of coolants with unprecedented thermal performance and energy efficiency. This perspective discusses how this framework could guide the design of next-generation coolants.

title: Dendrite genesis in structurally perfect solid electrolytes
abstract: Dendrites in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) have long been attributed to structural defects, yet they also emerge in defect-free, stiff electrolytes. We introduce the concept of "born unstable," in which infinitesimal interfacial perturbations are intrinsically amplified by electrochemo-mechanical coupling during the early stage of electrodeposition, without requiring pre-existing structural defects or heterogeneities in the solid electrolyte. This formulation exposes three universal pathways that govern interfacial stability: destabilizing electrochemical transport, stabilizing stress-driven ionic flux, and mechanics-modified reaction kinetics. By overturning the assumption that mechanical stiffness alone guarantees stability, the born unstable concept reframes interfacial safety as a coupled electrochemo-mechanical design problem rather than one dictated by stiffness alone. From this principle, we derive a predictive stability criterion that is validated against experimental observations across diverse electrolyte chemistries and operating regimes, shifting the field from post hoc interpretation toward mechanism-driven, proactive stabilization of ASSBs.

title: Emergence of colloidal nanocrystal near-infrared light-emitting diodes
abstract: Near-infrared light-emitting diodes (NIR-LEDs) have drawn great attention because of their broad applicability, including bioimaging, optical signal transmission, sensing, and night vision. Unlike traditional III–V semiconductors, colloidal nanocrystals (NCs) are now viewed as strong contenders for advanced NIR-LEDs by virtue of their solution processability, widely tunable emission spectra, and outstanding photophysical properties. This review surveys recent advances in NIR-LEDs from three representative colloidal nanocrystal systems: quantum dots, perovskite NCs, and colloidal quantum wells. It begins by introducing the device mechanisms of NIR-LEDs. Subsequently, the performance enhancement strategies are discussed from two perspectives: emissive layer optimization and device engineering. Emissive layer improvements focus on heterostructure design, composition control, and doping strategies. At the device level, advances in carrier-transport-layer engineering and interfacial modification are reviewed. Finally, the key challenges facing the field are outlined, and future research avenues are presented for rational design and practical application of high-performance NC-based NIR-LEDs.

title: Spatial configuration of MXene in MXene-rGO sponges enhances electromagnetic wave absorption
abstract: The unique electromagnetic properties of two-dimensional nanosheets have enabled their widespread application in electromagnetic absorbing materials, but the advantages brought by their size effect have also become bottlenecks for macroscopic applications. Traditional bottom-up assembly methods struggle to simultaneously achieve macro-scale (oriented, gradient, etc.) and micro-scale (self-restacking control, micro-morphology, etc.) design. Therefore, developing fabrication methods enabling cross-scale design of electromagnetic absorbers is crucial. Herein, we employ a sequential three-step approach of "layered freeze casting, molten-salt-assisted in situ synthesis, and mixed-acid in situ etching" to achieve cross-scale regulation of MXene within composite matrices, yielding rGMX n sponges with a hierarchical structure of "coral-like" MXene vertically anchored to an oriented rGO framework. The direction-selective electromagnetic absorption performance of the obtained rGMX n sponge is improved, exhibiting a high RL min of −74.19 dB for axial incidence and a broadband EAB of 8.29 GHz for radial incidence. Simultaneously, adjustable MXene content gradients enable target-frequency-specific absorption performance design, demonstrating substantial potential in lightweight electromagnetic protection.

title: Continuous refrigeration and dehumidification using the lower critical solution temperature cycle
abstract: Certain aqueous mixtures possess a lower critical solution temperature (LCST), such that when they are heated above the LCST, they separate into a water-rich and a water-scarce phase. This separation leads to a chemical potential difference once the two phases are cooled below the LCST, which can be utilized for various applications. In this work, we describe the thermodynamic theory of a heat-driven cycle based on aqueous LCST mixtures, which can be used for refrigeration and dehumidification. The reversible limits of these effects (maximum temperature drop and minimum indoor humidity) are derived and then calculated for an oleic acid, lidocaine, and water mixture. Furthermore, the LCST refrigeration and dehumidification cycles are demonstrated in a proof-of-concept system using this mixture as the working fluid. A temperature lift of ∼1°C and a humidity lift of 1 g/kg are measured, with the potential to increase performance through the discovery of LCST mixtures with a greater chemical potential difference between the phases and hybrid/multi-stage cycle architectures. Finally, we discuss other applications of LCST materials, including desalination and brine concentration.

title: Exploring magnesium- and calcium-based compounds via solid-state metathesis reactions
abstract: Magnesium- and calcium-based multinary compounds are pivotal in diverse scientific and technological applications. However, their syntheses particularly via conventional solid-state ceramic methods often require extreme conditions, such as high temperatures or pressures, and may only yield impurities instead of the desired materials. Here we report solid-state metathetical reactions involving predominantly chalcogen- and pnictogen-based honeycomb layered oxides (particularly the tellurates and antimonates) with alkaline-earth halides, nitrates or sulfates ( MgCl 2 , MgBr 2 · 6 H 2 O , MgSO 4 , Mg ( NO 3 ) 2 · 6 H 2 O , CaSO 4 · 2 H 2 O , Ca ( NO 3 ) 2 · 4 H 2 O , or CaCl 2 · 2 H 2 O ) at temperatures not exceeding 500 ° C to yield magnesium- and calcium-based materials previously achievable only under high-temperature or high-pressure conditions, as well as new metastable compounds exhibiting unique crystal versatility. Aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy was employed to provide detailed insights into their morphology, supplemented by diffraction and spectroscopic techniques. These results demonstrate that materials conventionally requiring gigapascal pressures or temperatures above 1,000 ° C can be synthesized at ambient pressure and significantly lower temperatures.

title: Matrix-guided recovery of FePO4 for battery materials from incineration sewage sludge ash
abstract: Recovering functional phosphate precursors from heterogeneous wastes is hindered by limited understanding of the relationships among matrix chemistry, phosphorus release, and downstream recovery. Here, a stage-resolved framework converts incineration sewage sludge ash (ISSA) into FePO 4 for battery materials through matrix-guided extraction, purification, and precipitation. Across biologically derived, Al-rich, and Fe-rich ISSA, phosphorus mobilization exhibited a three-stage pattern characterized by rapid Ca/Mg-associated release, Al-associated transition, and slower Fe-associated release. A system-dependent pH transition region was identified, above which phosphorus re-immobilization constrained recovery. Adjusting extraction conditions influences ion speciation in the extraction solution, while subsequent cation-exchange purification removes metal impurities and yields a purified phosphate-containing solution. Selective precipitation within a narrow pH window produces FePO 4 , which is subsequently converted into electrochemically functional LiFePO 4 /C. These results provide a physicochemical framework for understanding matrix-dependent phosphorus recovery and exhibit a route for converting complex waste streams into high-value battery precursor materials.

title: Chain-length effects and selectivity in alkaline polyol electrooxidation from glycerol to xylitol
abstract: Glycerol electro-oxidation is a promising way to utilise the oversupply from biodiesel production and simultaneously produce valuable organic acids as well as H2. Another promising bio-derived polyol for commodity chemicals production is xylitol, yet it has not attracted as much scientific attention as glycerol. The extensive studies on glycerol provide a good foundation for evaluating the reaction pathways of xylitol and for identifying molecular-size-dependent differences. In this study, we systematically investigate the influence of the polyol chain lengths of glycerol, erythritol, and xylitol on the electrooxidation and product distribution. We contrast the outcomes of using Pt and Ag electrodes for the anodic oxidation of these polyols in alkaline medium, as computational studies have shown a preference for carbonyl-C* adsorption on Pt and hydroxyl-O* adsorption on Ag, leading to different reaction paths and additional length-dependent effects. On Pt, we first observe a single oxidation process to the corresponding aldehyde. Subsequently, homogeneous CC bond cleavage of erythrose and xylose in the alkaline reaction media dominates the product outcome, while glyceraldehyde mainly yields C3 acids upon further oxidation. For Ag, we observe the formation of the same three acids, glyceric-, glycolic-and formic acid. Our findings indicate that direct CC cleavage occurs alongside oxidation, yielding one acid and one aldehyde in the first reaction step. Dependent on the polyol length, the ratios of the three resulting acids vary, providing valuable information about the preferred splitting behaviour. This study provides important insights into the electrooxidation of larger polyols than glycerol, with bearing on their suitability for selective chemicals production.

title: Rethinking circular food-contact materials by integrating safety, design, and regulation in closed-loop recycling
abstract: Circularity in food-contact materials is often inferred from recyclability, renewable origin, or material recovery, although none of these attributes alone demonstrates a safe and durable closed loop. Here, we report a framework that reframes food-contact circularity as an evidence-alignment problem across seven interdependent dimensions spanning feedstock control, material chemistry, processing, migration and analytical verification, regulation, system-level circulation, and environmental trade-offs. Applying this framework reveals that credible circularity emerges only when these dimensions converge: bottle-to-bottle polyethylene terephthalate and traceable polypropylene (PP)/HDPE loops currently show the strongest alignment, whereas consumer-loop polyolefins, multilayers, recyclable-by-design polymers, and bio-based systems remain limited by fragmented evidence. The dominant challenge is therefore not recovering material, but preserving chemical integrity, controlling non-intentionally added substances, validating repeated-cycle safety, and demonstrating regulatory and environmental viability. This framework provides a basis for separating demonstrated circularity from technically plausible but still aspirational recycling claims.

title: A mechanically robust high-index oxide-glass platform enabled by interchangeable seventh-principal-component design
abstract: Integrating mechanical robustness, high refractive index, and tunable optical functionality within a single oxide-glass framework remains challenging. Here, seven-principal-element oxide glasses with an ideal cation configurational entropy of 1.70 R are designed around a shared La 2 O 3 -Y 2 O 3 -Ta 2 O 5 -TiO 2 -ZrO 2 -Al 2 O 3 framework, with Gd 2 O 3 , Sm 2 O 3 , Eu 2 O 3 , or SrO introduced as an interchangeable seventh principal component. All compositions retain high hardness, Young's modulus, and indentation fracture toughness, together with refractive indices of approximately 1.91–1.98. Seventh component substitution further enables refractive-index enhancement, visible-to-near-infrared absorption, red emission, or high visible transmittance. Glass-forming behavior reflects the interplay between cation configurational entropy and cationic size disorder, as further indicated by the amorphous diffraction-peak width and thermal-stability window, whereas mechanical performance correlates with atomic packing density and composition-averaged dissociation energy density. This modular strategy establishes a mechanically robust high-index glass platform with compositionally selectable optical functions, providing a design route toward durable functional optical materials.

title: Fabrication of highly dye-loaded protein nanofibril films for UV shielding and down-conversion
abstract: Here, we report a simple yet innovative mechanochemical procedure to significantly increase the dispersion of fluorescent brightener 378 dye in aqueous solution without organic solvents by milling with hen egg white lysozyme protein and turning them into self-assembled dye functionalized nanofibrils. Free-standing films prepared from these functionalized nanofibrils efficiently block around 94% UV light (200–400 nm) with a total transparency around 90% at 600–700 nm. The films show excellent performance as UV filters for perovskite solar cells maintaining the original PCE of around 24% under harsh UV lighting conditions. The films show down conversion of UV light into deep-blue emission (400–500 nm) and subsequently used as fluorescent stickers. Finally, fully biogenic films are prepared from whey protein nanofibrils, showing similar optical and photophysical properties. The work presents novel methodology for efficient functionalization of low-cost protein materials with a high loading of hydrophobic dyes toward sustainable design of photonic materials.

title: Lignin depolymerization and carbohydrate preservation by linking selective fractionation to radical mechanisms
abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass (LCB) refining is constrained by the trade-off between fractionation efficiency and component preservation. Here, we report a synergistic fractionation approach applicable to chemically diverse feedstocks, including corn stover, bamboo, poplar, and pine. This strategy enables selective enrichment of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin, achieving cellulose retention above 88.6% and lignin removal exceeding 91.2%. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the alkaline hydrogen peroxide stage is governed by a radical-driven network, in which ·OH and O 2 − facilitate aromatic ring activation, side-chain oxidation, and selective β -O-4 cleavage while suppressing lignin condensation. The resulting lignin shows enhanced functional groups and structural uniformity. The cellulose fraction reaches a glucan conversion of 91.4%. The recovered lignin, with moderate molecular weight, narrow dispersity, and high phenolic hydroxy content, can be directly used as a pH-responsive emulsifier without modification. This study links macroscopic fractionation performance to microscopic radical mechanisms and provides a unified model for mechanism-guided LCB refining.

title: Structural and kinetic study of photoactivated modulation of lipid nanosystems via azobenzene functionalization
abstract: Here, we report the synthesis and characterization of three microfluidic-synthesized photoresponsive nanosystems, where three different azobenzene-based photoswitchable amphiphiles, namely a glycerophospholipid, a diacylglycerol, and a custom-designed single-tailed molecule, are intercalated in the lipid bilayer to obtain structural photomodulation. The reversible trans - cis isomerization of azobenzenes is exploited to trigger on/off switching of bilayer properties, i.e., packing and permeability, and the influence of different azobenzene molecular architecture on reversible bilayer properties is compared. UV-visible spectroscopy is used to monitor molecular photoisomerization, whereas supramolecular alterations of bilayer organization induced by photomodulation are characterized by dynamic light scattering and light-triggered, time-resolved small-angle X-ray scattering. This combination of techniques reveals insights into the spatial and temporal evolution of the bilayer structure occurring upon photoswitch activation; in particular, reversible or partially reversible structural transitions depend on the molecular architecture of the azobenzene switch.

title: Triple-cation perovskite solar cells show concentration-dependent defect passivation by phenethylammonium iodide
abstract: Incorporation of bulky organic ammonium additives into perovskite precursor solutions often induces low-dimensional phase formation, which can improve interfacial passivation but may hinder intrinsic charge-transport pathways. Here, we investigate the incorporation of low-concentration phenethylammonium iodide (PEAI) for suppressing defect-assisted recombination while preserving the predominantly three-dimensional (3D) perovskite framework in Cs 0.175 FA 0.750 MA 0.075 Pb(I 0.880 Br 0.120 ) 3 perovskite solar cells. The low-concentration regime is defined as PEAI concentrations of ≤0.75 wt %. Structural analyses show no detectable diffraction features associated with low-dimensional phases within this range. Optical and electrical analyses indicate reduced defect-assisted recombination, with the average carrier lifetime increasing from 94.53 to 206.46 ns and the trap density decreasing from 1.68 × 10 16 to 1.12 × 10 16 cm −3 . The 0.50 wt % PEAI device achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.98% and shows improved damp-heat (DH) stability relative to the control.

title: A modular in-incubator microscope for longitudinal live-cell microscopy
abstract: Longitudinal live cell imaging is valuable for characterizing dynamic morphological and phenotypic changes in biological systems. However, conventional approaches rely on manual microscope operation, which is labor-intensive, limits imaging frequency, and disrupts the cellular environment. These constraints reduce scalability, increase experimental variability, and restrict both the duration and temporal resolution of continuous imaging. Although automated imaging platforms partially address these limitations, existing solutions are often constrained by the cost, footprint, and inflexibility of in-incubator microscopes or stage-top incubators. Here, we present an automated in-incubator epifluorescence microscope designed for long-term operation. The system features a modular architecture with optional multi-fluorescence imaging, automated plate scanning, configurable light sources, and compatibility with multiple plate formats, including integration with fluidic automation devices. By positioning the light sources and control electronics outside the incubator, the platform improves thermal stability and long-term operational reliability. This approach enables continuous, high-frequency imaging over extended durations, providing a source of rich data for quantifying time-dependent tissue phenotypes, morphological remodeling, and transient biological processes.

title: Electronic modulation-driven Co-doped Ruddlesden-Popper for bifunctional OER/HER overall water splitting
abstract: Efficient and durable bifunctional electrocatalysts are needed for alkaline water splitting. Here, we report a d-LCCO-Ar catalyst that delivers high-performance oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity in 1 M KOH, requiring overpotentials of 190 and 122 mV, respectively, to reach 10 mA cm −2 and maintaining stability for 48 h. Its enhanced activity originates from A-site deficiency, partial Cu substitution by Co, and abundant oxygen vacancies (48.46%) formed by reductive Ar annealing. Compared with pristine LCO, d-LCCO-Ar shows a higher electrochemically active surface area, lower Tafel slopes, lower charge-transfer resistance, and higher turnover frequency (TOF). These results demonstrate an effective strategy for designing cost-effective, noble-metal-free electrocatalysts for alkaline overall water splitting.

title: Concentration-dependent effects from the permeation enhancers capric acid and SNAC on peptide permeability
abstract: Medium-chain fatty-acid-based permeation enhancers (PEs) can improve the oral bioavailability of peptide drugs through transcellular pathways, but their interactions with cell membranes and their effect on peptide permeability remain poorly understood. Here, we report coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations of two PEs, capric acid and salcaprozate sodium (SNAC), and their effects on membrane structure and peptide permeability. Capric acid acts in a concentration-dependent manner, substantially altering membrane structure and enhancing peptide permeability. SNAC instead shows a critical concentration above which its membrane incorporation saturates, causing its effect to plateau. SNAC resides in the interfacial head group region and protrudes into the aqueous phase, whereas capric acid partitions deeper into the bilayer. In these simulations, the computed effective permeability of the peptides is up to approximately four orders of magnitude higher with capric acid than with SNAC. These results highlight how molecular-level interaction patterns between PEs and membranes govern peptide drug delivery.

title: A microelectrode array-organoid interface for probing oscillatory behaviors and network-level functional characteristics in mini-brain models
abstract: The convergence of brain organoids and microelectrode arrays (MEAs) represents a transformative advancement in neuroscience, drug discovery, and the emerging field of organoid intelligence. However, the absence of refined analytical methods for extracting reliable and meaningful data continues to impede its full potential. By shifting from single-unit activity to local field potentials, we uncover the predominance of spatiotemporal slow oscillations, particularly within the delta range (<4 Hz), originating intrinsically from the organoids. Throughout development of the organoids, the intensity of oscillatory activity strongly correlates with neuronal maturity and cellular composition. Moreover, electrical or chemical stimulation can lead to rapid changes in oscillatory behavior. In ischemic stroke models, oxygen-glucose deprivation elicits changes in oscillatory patterns, accompanied by elevated delta-band coherence and increased global efficiency. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the oscillatory activity is associated with network-level functional connectivity across developmental and physiological states, providing insights into neural development, disease modeling, and biocomputing.

title: Developing stacking models for interacting biopolymers using quantum mechanical calculations and machine learning
abstract: Biopolymers are long-chain molecules with significant potential for developing sustainable, renewable, and environmentally friendly materials. Agarose, a biopolymer derived from red algae, is widely used in bioengineering and biomedical applications because of its biocompatibility and biodegradability. Understanding how agarose chains interact and assemble is essential for explaining its gelation behavior and material properties. For decades, scientists have debated whether agarose chains primarily form double-helical structures or other arrangements. In this study, researchers used high-throughput quantum mechanical calculations and machine-learning models to investigate the interactions between agarose chains. Their results show that stacked configurations are energetically and statistically more favorable than the traditionally proposed double-helix structure. The study also identifies simple interatomic interactions and distances between specific atomic species as effective descriptors for predicting the assembled structures. These findings resolve a long-standing controversy and provide valuable insight into agarose structure, gelation, and the design of advanced biopolymeric materials.

title: Non-destructive colocalization sensing of microRNAs and membrane proteins in single vesicles reveals spatial inflammation signatures
abstract: Chronic inflammation underlies a broad spectrum of diseases, yet current liquid biopsy approaches lack the spatial resolution and molecular specificity to detect localized, disease-specific inflammatory signals. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) offer a promising alternative, as they carry both membrane proteins and intravesicular biomolecules that reflect the physiological state and tissue of origin. Here, we present a sensing platform for single-vesicle colocalization analysis of membrane proteins and microRNAs (miRNAs), using cellulose nanofiber-mediated membrane fusion to non-destructively deliver probes into intact EVs. This approach enables simultaneous detection of tissue-specific and inflammation-associated markers in individual EVs. In kidney transplant recipients with chronic active antibody-mediated rejection, we identify EVs co-expressing the renal marker DPYS and miR-1246. In rheumatoid arthritis patients, we observe elevated levels of miR-1246 + /CD81 + EVs in plasma. Our platform distinguishes among inflammation-related EV subpopulations that are undetectable using bulk or surface-only analyses, thereby offering a non-invasive strategy for localized inflammation profiling.

title: A lean statistical cell-to-pack framework for sustainable battery pack capacity estimation
abstract: Accurate battery pack capacity estimation is vital for electric vehicle and energy storage safety, but conventional pack-level aging tests are costly, energy intensive, and wasteful. This study proposes a lean statistical cell-to-pack (LS-CTP) framework that eliminates pack-level tests. Using aging data from only a few independent test cells, it combines lightweight machine learning and decision algorithms to achieve multi-feature statistical transformation and fusion from routine fragmented charge data. It requires few hyperparameters and low computational overhead and applies to parallel, series, and mixed configurations. Monte Carlo analyses show a mean absolute percentage error below 1.24% for parallel packs and 1.92% for series packs using as few as two test cells. A sustainability assessment indicates over 90% reduction in battery waste and testing energy. By decoupling algorithm development from pack-level cycling, LS-CTP advances cost-effective, energy-efficient, and sustainable battery health diagnostics, supporting the clean energy transition.

title: Surface acoustic waves drive interfacial fragmentation in porous fibrous solids
abstract: Surface acoustic waves provide a surface-confined route for activating dry, compliant porous solids, but their coupling through direct solid-solid contact remains poorly understood. Here, we use compressed plant-derived fiber networks as a model system. Compared with conductive heating and combustion, surface acoustic wave excitation generates stable particulate plumes at approximately 150°C–210°C with only 8%–9% mass loss. Particle-size measurements reveal a reproducible fine-particle mode of 1–2.5 μm and, at stronger excitation, an additional coarse fraction near 35 μm. Post-treatment microscopy shows pronounced fiber network disruption and interfacial debris, while in situ microscopy captures interfacial restructuring and discrete fiber fracture during excitation. These observations show that bulk temperature alone cannot account for the release behavior and support an interface-confined acousto-thermo-mechanical response in which acoustothermal dissipation and contact-mediated mechanical excitation jointly promote localized fragmentation and particulate detachment.

title: In situ, operando, and transient approaches to understanding dynamic catalytic interfaces
abstract: Catalytic processes are inherently dynamic. These processes take place at various timescales and length scales, necessitating direct observation of interfaces and their local environments under realistic operating conditions. This Voices piece brings together researchers from around the world across all areas of catalysis to comment on the opportunities and challenges of collecting in situ, operando, and transient measurements.

title: Emerging and transformative applications of tissue clearing technology in neuroscience research
abstract: Refractive index (RI)-matching-based tissue clearing techniques render intact biological tissues optically transparent, enabling 3D in situ interrogation of nervous systems from whole-brain to single-cell scales. We systematically evaluate three mainstream clearing strategies (hydrophobic, hydrophilic, and hydrogel-based) and summarize their promising applications in neural circuit tracing, tumor research, stem cell therapy, and artificial intelligence (AI) integration. Here, we report that this technology has evolved from a niche imaging tool to an integrated multimodal biotechnological platform. Despite core challenges, including inherent physicochemical trade-offs, optical limits, multi-omics integration biases, and insufficient clinical standardization, future advances in multimodal integration, AI algorithms, and targeted in vivo clearing will drive life science research from static structural mapping toward systematic dissection of dynamic biological processes.

title: Structural variation of cooling and heating energy demand with degree-day estimation method
abstract: Degree-day methods are essential for estimating building heating and cooling energy demands. We investigate the sensitivity of cooling and heating degree-day models, CDD26 and HDD18, at national and regional scales across mainland China. Non-observational datasets overestimate national heating demand while severely underestimating cooling demand. Compared with current building codes, substituting estimation indicators and calculation models amplifies national cooling demand by 29.7%–100.6%, whereas national heating demand variations are −5.6% to 1.8%. Estimation methods prominently affect cooling demand in hot-summer zones, fundamentally reshaping the cooling energy structures of HSCWZ and CZ. While heating demand in warmer zones exhibits higher sensitivity to estimation indicators and calculation models, this sensitivity does not alter their overarching heating energy structures. Structurally, ASHRAE's T avg formulation increases indicator variability, whereas UKMO mitigates this variability but systematically inflates CDD26 and HDD18. T avg benchmarking paired with asymmetric T max and T min dominant coefficients structurally control degree-day sensitivity across calculation models.

title: Heterogeneity propagation and surface homogenization for pouch-cell-sized Li metal anodes
abstract: Li metal batteries are challenged by anode instability issues originating from Li surface utilization heterogeneities, which emerge during the earliest stages of cycling, propagate throughout operation, and ultimately drive cell-to-cell performance variations and failure. However, heterogeneity issues remain under-investigated due to mainstream studies' reliance on electrodes with small areas and few replicates. Here, we evaluated 32 Li || NMC811 pouch cells, using either as-purchased or mechanically homogenized Li via brushing. The brushed group exhibits narrower distributions of capacity trajectories and lifetimes, along with a 35% increase in median lifetime relative to the as-purchased group. Additionally, millimeter-scale variations in chemical compositions are observed on the as-purchased Li surface and result in localized utilization patterns after initial plating and stripping, whereas such inhomogeneity is eliminated after brushing. This work establishes a link between early-stage Li utilization and cell performance consistency, providing a pathway for evaluating and improving reliability in large-format battery production.

title: Toward standard testing methods in biophotovoltaics based on cyanobacteria
abstract: Microbial biophotovoltaics (BPVs) are an emerging renewable energy technology that harnesses photosynthetic microorganisms to generate electric current. Despite the rapid growth of the field, the lack of standardized testing and reporting methods currently prevents the benchmarking of devices, slowing technological progress. This article provides a critical analysis of the experimental practices used in BPV research, highlighting the significant variability in device configurations, light sources, electrode materials, biomass quantification methods, and electrochemical measurement protocols reported in the literature. It further considers the historical standardization of protocols for conventional photovoltaics (PVs) and the resulting acceleration of the maturation and market adoption of PV technologies. Drawing inspiration from conventional PVs, the article outlines key steps toward BPV standardization, including defining common testing conditions, methods for data normalization, shared reference systems, and round-robin testing protocols. Establishing consensus in the testing protocols would significantly improve reproducibility and enable meaningful comparisons across laboratories, accelerating the development and deployment of BPVs.

title: Selenium-engineered self-assembling protein nanoparticles rescue synaptic integrity and cognition via ferroptosis inhibition in Alzheimer’s mice
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common neurodegenerative disorder, yet effective disease-modifying therapies remain elusive. Here, we apply a semantic logic framework of Gene Ontology-based protein function prediction to identify ferroptosis-inhibitory proteins with potential neuroprotective activity. Guided by these predictions, we engineer selenium-modified apolipoprotein A1 supramolecular nanoparticles (Se-NDs) that intrinsically display glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4)-like catalytic activity and exhibit high brain penetrance. Se-ND suppresses lipid peroxidation, restores redox balance, and blocks ferroptotic neuronal death, thereby promoting mitochondrial repair and synaptic integrity and reversing structural and functional deficits underlying cognitive decline. Moreover, Se-ND synergizes with anti-inflammatory interventions and other AD-associated pathways. Our findings identify ferroptosis inhibition as a critical disease-modifying mechanism and establish Se-ND as a promising therapeutic avenue for Alzheimer's disease.

title: Tailoring bandgap and electron affinity of spacecraft dielectrics for synergistic solar array charging and discharge suppression
abstract: As the core power source for spacecraft in orbit, the reliability of solar arrays (SAs) critically determines mission success. However, the increasingly severe spacecraft charging-discharging issue under complex space environments restricts next-generation high-voltage, high-power spacecraft. Current mitigation strategies rely largely on process-based measures such as adhesive coating, while the physical mechanisms and a material-based mitigation framework remain underexplored. We systematically investigate the roles of the bandgap and electron affinity of coverglasses in SAs during surface charging-discharging using theoretical modeling, numerical simulation, and experimental validation. Under high-energy electron irradiation, bandgap governs internal secondary electron generation, whereas electron affinity controls true secondary electron emission. Increasing both reduces surface charging potential differences and suppresses secondary electron yield, mitigating electrostatic discharge risk. This work reveals intrinsic links between material band parameters and charging-discharging dynamics, offering guidance for dielectric material selection and modification in high-power spacecraft.

title: Regioselective meta-C−H borylation of aryl acetic acid derivatives enabled by iridium-aluminum bifunctional catalysts
abstract: Remote C–H functionalization provides a powerful strategy for overcoming the inherent selectivity of arene functionalization. While reversible secondary-sphere interactions have enabled remote regioselective borylation of benzoic acid derivatives, analogous transformations of phenylacetic acid derivatives and higher homologs remain largely unexplored because increased distance from the directing group disfavors metallamacrocyclic transition states. Herein, we report bifunctional iridium catalysts featuring a tunable Lewis-acidic aluminum site in the secondary coordination sphere for highly selective remote meta -C–H borylation of phenylacetamides. Systematic ligand engineering further enables borylation of previously inaccessible arylpropanamides, arylbutanamides, and aryloxyacetamides. The distinct regioselectivity from the conventional [Ir(cod)(OMe)] 2 /dtbpy system highlights the decisive roles of Lewis acid-base interactions and bifunctional catalyst design. Gram-scale synthesis, downstream diversification, and late-stage functionalization of napropamide and ketoprofen demonstrate the method's synthetic utility. Control experiments and DFT studies elucidate the ligand design and the crucial role of aluminum Lewis acidity in controlling selectivity.

title: Autonomous top-perching with an asymmetric bistable claw
abstract: Long-duration in situ observation in constrained natural environments (e.g., caves and dense arboreal canopies) is crucial for ecological monitoring. While unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) provide cross-terrain access, their operational feasibility is limited by substantial power demands and acoustic disturbance from sustained hovering. Here, we present an autonomous top-perching UAV system that leverages overhead structures for stable suspension and enhanced adaptability in confined spaces. The system features a foldable, asymmetric bistable mechanism. By modulating the structural asymmetry to tailor its energy landscape, it maintains a compact flight configuration (8:1 folding ratio), while achieving rapid, low-energy deployment (0.16 s) into a strong load-bearing state for stable perching. Indoor and outdoor experiments demonstrate the system's ability to perch on diverse natural structures, including trees, drilling holes, cavities, and rock wall gaps. These capabilities demonstrate how mechanical intelligence can simplify aerial interaction tasks, extending the operational scope of autonomous aerial systems in unstructured environments.

title: From sequence to function: Peptide-nucleotide-based complex coacervates as protocell models
abstract: Complex coacervates formed through the liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of peptides and nucleotide-based biomolecules have emerged as versatile model systems for understanding biomolecular self-assembly, compartmentalization, and emergent functionality. This review highlights recent advances in peptide-nucleotide-based complex coacervates, encompassing nucleotide motifs and nucleic acids in combination with peptides and polypeptides. We discuss the molecular features that drive phase separation, including multivalency, sequence, and charge distribution. We further examine how internal organization and responsiveness to external stimuli enable precise control over the physicochemical properties and functions of coacervate droplets. Their intrinsic capabilities, including compartmentalization, selective molecular sequestration, and catalysis, provide compelling opportunities for developing life-like assemblies with emergent biological functions. Finally, we highlight key conceptual gaps and future challenges that could guide the development of coacervates as functional materials at the interface of synthetic biology and chemistry.

title: Ionic hydrogel sensors for low-latency high-accuracy 3D reconstruction of soft robotic endoscope
abstract: Continuous shape sensing remains a major barrier to deploying soft robotic endoscopes, because existing solutions often compromise structural compliance, require expensive instrumentation, or provide only limited embedded feedback. Here, we report an integrated soft sensing system based on an array of ionic hydrogel strain sensors, enabling low-latency, high-accuracy three-dimensional shape reconstruction of a soft endoscope tip. Optimization across NaCl concentration, applied voltage, and strain rate identifies ideal composition and operating conditions jointly balancing gauge factor, strain-rate independence, and mechanical robustness. Three optimized sensors are then integrated around the circumference of a soft pneumatic actuator, addressing adhesion, dehydration, and signal stability under actuation. Continuous three-dimensional shape reconstruction is achieved using a Frenet-Serret-based model, and a simple delay-compensation strategy reduces the relative tip-position error from 10.08% to 5.92% of the actuator arc length. This offers a low-cost, compliant, disposable-compatible route to proprioceptive sensing for minimally invasive intervention.

title: Multi-state surface engineering improves Phi29 solubility, thermostability, and low-input amplification
abstract: Phi29 DNA polymerase is widely used for isothermal whole-genome amplification but is limited by low-salt aggregation, modest thermostability, and inconsistent performance with low-input DNA.
