Here, we developed a multi-state surface-charge engineering workflow that combines Pythia-based stability scoring with AlphaFold3 structural filtering across apo and DNA-bound states. Screening solvent-exposed aromatic residues yielded two matched eight-site variants, Phi29-M1 and Phi29-M2. Both variants retained rolling circle amplification activity while showing approximately 3-fold higher soluble recovery under low-salt stress, 2°C–3°C higher melting temperatures, and 2- to 3-fold stronger DNA binding, mainly through faster association. In multiple-displacement amplification, M1 and M2 generated usable low-template input (10 pg) products at 30°C–37°C under conditions where wild-type Phi29 failed. Molecular dynamics simulations were consistent with reduced flexibility around the exonuclease-palm and fingers-side tunnel regions. Together, these findings support the potential utility of multi-site surface engineering for improving Phi29 robustness in low-input genomic applications.

title: Electrochemical memory in LiFePO4 batteries arises from diffusion-driven dynamical asymmetry
abstract: Voltage relaxation in lithium-ion batteries reflects internal electrochemical states but is generally assumed to follow a unique history-independent pathway toward equilibrium. From paired relaxation experiments on LiFePO 4 cells over broad states of health, we show that this assumption is incomplete. Relaxation exhibits "electrochemical memory," a measurable trajectory-level property of nonequilibrium battery relaxation dependent on the charge/discharge history. It shows a robust nonmonotonic dependence on state of charge (SOC), with reduced memory at ∼50%–70% SOC, and an increase toward low and high SOCs. After controlling for SOC, we show that electrochemical memory remains strongly associated with transport-related dynamical asymmetry, supporting a diffusion-mediated interpretation of the observed behavior. Reconstructed phase-space analyses reveal persistent organization of history-dependent relaxation trajectories, while trajectory recoverability demonstrates electrochemical memory encoded throughout relaxation. Overall, voltage relaxation is redefined as an electrochemical-history nonequilibrium dynamical process. Our trajectory-centric framework enables the investigation of electrochemical memory, nonequilibrium battery dynamics, and physics-informed battery diagnostics.

title: Intrinsic selectivity in fiber/textile-based multimodal sensors: Materials, architectures, and design principles
abstract: With the rapid development of flexible electronics and wearable technologies, fiber/textile-based multimodal flexible sensors have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation smart textiles. Owing to their softness, breathability, deformability, skin conformability, and compatibility with scalable textile manufacturing, these sensors show great potential in health monitoring, human-machine interaction, soft robotics, and personalized wearable systems. However, the hierarchical structure of textile materials makes multimodal sensing more complex than simple functional integration, as different stimuli can induce coupled structural and electrical responses, resulting in signal overlap and crosstalk. To promote the practical application and better development of multimodal smart textiles, this review summarizes recent progress in fiber/textile-based multimodal sensors from the perspective of structure-enabled selective sensing. The intrinsic coupling mechanisms, structural design principles, and integration strategies are reviewed to clarify how textile structures can be engineered for selective response, reduced interference, and improved sensing reliability. This review further discusses the current challenges and future development trends of multimodal smart textiles, including robust sensing, scalable fabrication, system integration, and wearable reliability. Overall, this review aims to provide useful guidance for researchers in materials science, textile engineering, flexible electronics, and wearable systems and to inspire the development of next-generation multimodal smart textiles with intrinsic selectivity and practical applicability.

title: Mechanical energy as a programmable redox input enables boronic acid activation for direct C–H functionalization of heteroarenes
abstract: The development of sustainable strategies for radical-mediated C–H functionalization is essential for greener synthesis. Herein, we demonstrate that mechanical energy can serve as a programmable redox stimulus through the piezoelectric properties of BaTiO 3 , enabling mechanoredox C–H arylation and alkylation of heteroarenes under vibratory shaker mill conditions. Mechanical agitation transiently polarizes BaTiO 3 , promoting persulfate activation to generate sulfate radicals that convert aryl and alkyl boronic acids into carbon-centered radicals. The transition-metal-free, solvent-minimized protocol affords diverse functionalized heteroarenes with excellent functional group tolerance and enables late-stage diversification of active pharmaceutical ingredients, ligand scaffolds, and materials-relevant intermediates. The method is scalable, while BaTiO 3 can be recovered and reused over multiple cycles. Mechanistic studies support a sulfate-radical-mediated pathway analogous to Minisci chemistry. Overall, this work establishes recyclable piezoelectric materials and mechanical energy as a sustainable platform for radical C–H functionalization.

title: A critical audit and methodological roadmap for machine learning in perovskite solar cells
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have advanced from 3.8% to 27.01% power conversion efficiency (PCE) in 17 years, while their lead-free analogs have reached 17.1%, and perovskite/silicon tandems exceeded 34%. Machine learning (ML) is credited with accelerating much of this progress, yet its evaluation is rarely examined. Here, we report a critical audit of 80 ML-PSC studies from 2024 to 2026. Among these, 89% report no error analysis on any sub-range of PCE, none report nested cross-validation, 48% rely on a single train/test split, and only 9% predict stability over time. Models that appear accurate overall can therefore fail in the sparse high-PCE region, which is the region most relevant to commercialization. We reframe high-PCE prediction as an imbalanced regression problem, establish imbalance-aware techniques, recommend an evaluation workflow, and propose a five-pillar roadmap. Further progress depends as much on shared evaluation and reporting standards as on new algorithms.

title: Designing strategies of photothermal membranes for membrane distillation
abstract: Photothermal membrane distillation (PMD) has emerged as a promising solar-driven desalination technology by enabling localized interfacial heating to overcome the energy limitations of conventional membrane distillation (MD). This review summarizes recent advances in photothermal membranes for MD applications, focusing on photothermal materials and membrane architectures. The roles of plasmonic metals, semiconductor nanostructures, carbon-based materials, conjugated polymers, MXenes, and metal-organic frameworks are discussed in terms of photothermal mechanisms, structure-property relationships, and design considerations. Membrane fabrication strategies, including surface coating, blending, freestanding structures, and hierarchical architectures, are evaluated regarding light absorption, heat localization, hydrophobicity, and vapor transport. Representative PMD membrane performances are compared, and key challenges including long-term stability, scalability, and standardized evaluation are highlighted. Future perspectives, such as additive manufacturing, hybrid systems, and data-driven optimization, are discussed to guide the development of practical PMD technologies.

title: Aromatic tripeptide predicted insoluble displays highest known solubility
abstract: Despite the fundamental importance of solubility, this key physical property remains only partially understood, and its prediction often fails to reproduce experimentally measured values. Here, we systematically investigate the solubility of aromatic amino acids and their dipeptides to hexapeptide oligomers. Remarkably, tyrosyl-tyrosyl-tyrosine tripeptide (YYY) exhibits an unprecedented solubility of ∼10,090 mg/mL, nearly five orders of magnitude higher than its monomeric counterpart (∼0.5 mg/mL), approximately 21 times higher than glucose (∼479 mg/mL) and 13 times higher than fructose (∼778 mg/mL), thereby establishing YYY as the most soluble organic solid reported. Chemical modification of YYY termini significantly reduces its solubility, indicating the native structure singularity. The remarkable solubility of a simple peptide allows the development of highly soluble organic materials with applications across science and engineering.

title: Ynamide β-hydroselenization and β-hydrosulfuration enable sequential selenocysteine/cysteine editing in peptides and proteins
A feasibility demonstration of integrated deionization and electrolysis for portable hydrogen production from seawater
